title: Release-evidence gate step cannot fail: check_frontend_release.py is run without --require-complete
description: The 'Frontend release evidence contracts' step runs `python3 tool/check_frontend_release.py docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json` with no `--require-complete` flag. In tool/check_frontend_release.py `validate()` only raises on malformed metadata; `main()` returns 0 whenever the document parses, printing 'release NOT complete: ...' as an info line. With every required check in 09-release-candidate.json at PENDING (and even if some were FAIL) the step is green. Running it now prints 'Manifest valid; release NOT complete: accessibility, automated, deployment-smoke, device-lifecycle, layout, performance, real-maps, secondary-screens, trip-journeys' and exits 0. docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md presents this as a merge/release gate, but the only thing it blocks is a syntactically broken JSON file.
failure_scenario: A release candidate with FAIL or PENDING evidence rows passes the verify job, deploy-pages.yml (workflow_run on 'Drider CI' success, main) then publishes the web build to GitHub Pages although the evidence manifest says the release is not complete.
evidence: .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:55 `python3 tool/check_frontend_release.py docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json`; tool/check_frontend_release.py:54 `if require_complete and incomplete:` ... :75 `return 0`; local run output: `Manifest valid; release NOT complete: accessibility, ... trip-journeys` / `exit=0`
suggested_fix: Either pass `--require-complete` in the CI step (and only on release branches/tags if PENDING must be allowed on PRs), or make a FAIL status a hard error regardless of the flag.

title: DECISIONS.md documents contract v0.3.0 while the code, tests and contracts/contract.json are v0.4.0
description: The decisions record says the source of truth is contracts/contract.json 'v0.3.0, copied byte-for-byte' (lines 26, 103) and refers to 'Contract v0.3'. contracts/contract.json line 3 is `"version": "0.4.0"` and test/contract/contract_copy_test.dart:39-43 asserts `"version": "0.4.0"` and `TripTransitions.contractVersion == '0.4.0'`. The documented intent and the enforced version disagree; per the audit rules, code that does not match the docs is a defect (here the docs are stale, which misleads reviewers about which shared contract the Driver app is pinned to).
failure_scenario: A reviewer syncing the contract from upstream reads DECISIONS.md, re-syncs v0.3.0 and breaks contract_copy_test / the Rider-Driver realtime kinds added in 0.4.0.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:26 `contracts/contract.json (v0.3.0, copied byte-for-byte; see "Contract v0.3" below)`; :103 `shared Movera contract v0.3.0`; contracts/contract.json:3 `"version": "0.4.0"`; test/contract/contract_copy_test.dart:39-43
suggested_fix: Update DECISIONS.md to v0.4.0 and add a doc/contract consistency check or a changelog entry for the 0.3 → 0.4 bump.

title: DECISIONS.md records a 20 m web GPS filter and a 5 Hz marker throttle; the code uses distanceFilter 0 on every platform and pushes the live marker every frame from a 33 ms ticker
description: The 'Active ride crash recovery (Safari / PWA)' decision says: `Map markers update on a 5Hz throttle ... GPS setState is gone; web GPS filter is 20m.` The trip subscribes with `watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)` for all platforms (`accept_ride_trip.dart:605`), and `DriverLocationService._streamSettings` forwards that 0 unchanged on web (`driver_location_service.dart:60-66`), so every browser callback reaches `_applyDriverPosition`; no 20 m filter exists anywhere in lib/ (grep for distanceFilter shows only 0 and 8). The marker path is `_ThrottledVehicleMap` with `Timer.periodic(33 ms)` (~30 Hz) feeding a `ValueNotifier<Marker?>` that `CustomGoogleMap._onLiveMarker` flushes once per frame via `GoogleMapsFlutterPlatform.instance.updateMarkers` (`custom_google_map.dart:216-243`), not 5 Hz. The later D-07/D-08 design (no widget rebuild per fix) is what prevents the Safari rebuild crash, so this is doc drift rather than a regression, but the decision record now describes guards that are not in the build.
failure_scenario: An engineer reading DECISIONS.md believes web GPS is rate-limited to 20 m moves and markers to 5 Hz; on web every geolocation callback and up to 30 marker updates per second actually reach the map and the island (`NavigationController.setVehicle` → `notifyListeners`).
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:85: `- Map markers update on a 5Hz throttle with a stable ValueKey('active-ride-map'). GPS setState is gone; web GPS filter is 20m.` accept_ride_trip.dart:604-605: `_positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)`. driver_location_service.dart:60-66: `if (kIsWeb || !navigation) { return LocationSettings(accuracy: ..., distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters); }`. accept_ride.dart:1458: `_ticker = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 33), (_) {`.
suggested_fix: Either reinstate the documented web filter/throttle (e.g. `distanceFilterMeters: kIsWeb ? 20 : 0` and a 200 ms ticker) or update DECISIONS.md to describe the D-07/D-08 per-frame live-marker design.

title: Documented browser-key referrer restriction names a different Pages path than the one the deploy workflow actually serves
description: PRIVACY_SECURITY.md instructs the owner to restrict the Maps browser key to HTTP referrer `https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/Movera-drider-/*` (and BASELINE.md:5 names the repo `Movera-drider-`), but the git remote is `github.com/baccarisverige-ux/Movera-driver-app` and deploy-pages.yml builds with `--base-href "/Movera-driver-app/"`, so the live demo is served from `https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/Movera-driver-app/`. The owner action the document prescribes is the only safeguard for a public key (the comment in web/index.html:37-39 relies on it); if followed literally it would block the real site with RefererNotAllowedMapError, and if the owner instead leaves the key unrestricted to keep the site working, the key is open to any origin. Either way the record does not describe the deployed artefact.
failure_scenario: Owner applies the documented referrer restriction `.../Movera-drider-/*` in Cloud Console -> the deployed site at `/Movera-driver-app/` loads the Maps script, Google rejects it, driverMapCamera.ready() never becomes true (see the blank-map finding) and the demo map is dead; alternatively the restriction is skipped and the public key stays usable from any site.
evidence: docs/PRIVACY_SECURITY.md:33 `1. Application restriction: HTTP referrers, limited to https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/Movera-drider-/*, plus any production domain.`; .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml:84 `run: flutter build web --release --base-href "/Movera-driver-app/" --dart-define=MOVERA_DEMO_ARRIVAL=true`; `git remote -v` -> `origin https://github.com/baccarisverige-ux/Movera-driver-app`
suggested_fix: Update PRIVACY_SECURITY.md (and BASELINE.md) to the current repository/Pages path, and record the applied restriction in the release evidence matrix.

title: Gate doc says verify runs `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`; workflow runs `--fatal-infos`
description: docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md describes the verify job as running `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, but .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:47 runs `flutter analyze --fatal-infos`. The documented policy and the enforced policy differ: contributors following the doc locally will pass analysis with info-level diagnostics that then fail CI.
failure_scenario: Developer runs the documented command locally, sees no errors, pushes; the verify job fails on an info-level lint.
evidence: docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:33 `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`; .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:47 `run: flutter analyze --fatal-infos`
suggested_fix: Align the doc with the workflow (or vice versa).

title: Camera architecture doc states a 72% anchor, zoom levels 17.5/16.5/15.5/14.75, explore zoom 16.8, 45° following tilt, 17.8/20° maneuver framing and a 35 m arrival flatten; the code uses 75%, 15/14.5/14/13.625, 11.7, tilt-follows-zoom to 67.5°, turnZoom 15.4 and a 140 m ease to 60°, and the web verifier asserts the doc's 0.72 rather than the app's 0.75
description: The document that the audit is told to treat as the record of intent no longer matches the shipped policy. Anchor: doc says `The driving anchor is 72% of screen height`; the trip passes `cameraAnchor: ... ? .75 : .5` (`accept_ride.dart:1234`), `MapOverlayInsets.drivingInsets` uses `height * .75` (`map_overlay_insets.dart:34`) and `CustomGoogleMap` documents `.75 drives` (`custom_google_map.dart:60`). `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:362` and `:615` exercise `configure(..., .72)`, so the verifier checks the documented value, not the one the app sends. Zoom/tilt: doc lines 47-50 give Auto Zoom 17.5/16.5/15.5/14.75, maneuver zoom 17.8 with tilt easing to 20°, and `Last 35 m flattens for arrival`; the code has `zoomForSpeed` 15 → 13.625 (`driver_camera_controller.dart:198-209`), `turnZoom = 15.4` with tilt rising via `tiltForZoom` (189-191, 325), `arrivalMeters = 140`, `arrivalZoom = 15.5`, `arrivalTilt = 60` (194-196) and the comment `never flat`. Modes table: `Explore ... neighborhood zoom 16.8` vs `exploreZoom = 11.7` (line 92); `Following | Heading-up, 45 degrees` vs tilt from the zoom curve up to 67.5. The code comments make clear the newer numbers are the owner's intent, so the doc is stale.
failure_scenario: Acceptance/device testers use the architecture doc as the spec (e.g. expect a 72% anchor or a flat arrival) and either pass wrong behaviour or fail correct behaviour; the CI web verifier gives no signal if the app's 0.75 anchor diverges from the doc.
evidence: docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:35-36: `The driving anchor is **72% of screen height**`; :47-50: `Auto Zoom defaults on: 17.5 below 20 km/h, 16.5 at 20–50, 15.5 at 50–80, 14.75 above 80. Inside 180 m of significant maneuvers, zoom tightens toward 17.8 and tilt eases toward 20 degrees ... Last 35 m flattens for arrival.`; :30: `Explore | Driver-centered, north-up, flat, neighborhood zoom 16.8`. accept_ride.dart:1233-1234: `cameraAnchor: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following ? .75 : .5,`. driver_camera_controller.dart:92: `static const double exploreZoom = 11.7;`; :189: `static const double turnZoom = 15.4;`; :194-196: `arrivalMeters = 140; arrivalZoom = 15.5; arrivalTilt = 60;`. tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:362: `api.configure(7, 100, 200, .72);`.
suggested_fix: Update the Modes table, anchor percentage and zoom/tilt numbers in docs/driver-camera-architecture.md to the current constants, and have the verifier assert the anchor value the app actually passes (0.75).

title: ReservationRequestPreview.pickupAt is one hour off on daylight-saving switch days (adds minutes as absolute Duration to local midnight)
description: `pickupAt` builds the pickup instant as `DateTime(y, m, d + offset).add(Duration(minutes: minuteOfDay))`. `DateTime.add` adds absolute time, so when the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' date is a DST transition day in the zone (Sweden/France: last Sunday of March and October) the wall-clock result is shifted by an hour relative to the 'HH:mm' label. Reproduced with `TZ=Europe/Stockholm`: for 'Tomorrow 07:40' on 24 Oct 2026 the code yields 2026-10-25 06:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 12h40); on 28 Mar 2026 it yields 08:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 10h40). `untilPickup`, the 'leave now'/'go online for' island timers (home_scheduled.dart:94-131, 321-342), the Scheduled-rides sort (scheduled_rides.dart:630-632) and `SmartGap` clash detection (smart_gap.dart:67-68) all consume this value.
failure_scenario: On Sunday 25 Oct 2026 (DST ends) a driver has a reservation 'Today 07:40'. The island says 'Leave now' and the reminder fires an hour early (06:40), and the countdown reads 1 h less than the clock; on 29 Mar it is an hour late, so 'leave now' appears after the pickup time.
evidence: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 `return DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset)\n        .add(Duration(minutes: minute));` · scratch run output: `Tomorrow 07:40 (DST ends 25 Oct): pickupAt()=2026-10-25 06:40:00.000 expected=2026-10-25 07:40:00.000` / `(DST starts 29 Mar): pickupAt()=2026-03-29 08:40:00.000 expected=07:40`
suggested_fix: Construct the wall-clock time directly: `DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset, minute ~/ 60, minute % 60)`.

title: _DemoReservationSet._at labels a next-day demo reservation 'Today' on the spring DST day
description: Same pattern as scheduled_rides_notes.dart: `DateTime(at.y,m,d).difference(DateTime(anchor.y,m,d)).inDays` is 0 across the 23-hour spring-forward day, so `days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow'` yields 'Today' for a ride that is actually tomorrow. The resulting pickupDay feeds `pickupAt` (offset 0 instead of 1), so the demo reservation's countdown and clash logic are a full day off on that day. Demo seed data only (DemoReservations), hence low.
failure_scenario: Demo launched late on 28 March with a reservation lead that lands after midnight: Scheduled rides and the island show it as 'Today HH:mm' and its untilPickup is already negative, so it never becomes a 'Leave now' trip.
evidence:
lib/core/admin/driver_home_admin_content.dart:492-495 `final days = DateTime(at.year, at.month, at.day)
        .difference(DateTime(anchor.year, anchor.month, anchor.day))
        .inDays;
    return build(clockLabel(at), days == 0 ? 'Today' : 'Tomorrow');`
suggested_fix: Compare calendar dates (e.g. `DateTime.utc(at.year, at.month, at.day).difference(DateTime.utc(anchor.year, ...)).inDays`).

title: A fresh Idempotency-Key is generated on every request, so a retry after a lost response is a new mutation instead of a replay
description: The contract (contract.json#headers, openapi IdempotencyKey: 'the same key replays the committed response', DriverCommand doc 'Reuse it on retry') makes the key the only way to recover from a committed-but-unanswered mutation. `_headers(mutation: true)` calls `_key()` (a random 32-hex string) each time it is invoked, and `claimOffer`/`declineOffer` call `_headers` per HTTP request with no key kept per offer/attempt. On a transport exception `claimOffer` returns `networkError`; Home/Ride requests then let the driver tap Match again (home_offer_radar.dart:559-564, ride_requests.dart:338-341), which sends the same body under a new key. If the first POST had been committed server-side (response lost), the second accept is a separate command against an offer this driver already holds; the server answers 409 (invalid_transition/conflict with the offer, status != open/claimed_elsewhere), and the 409 branch (lines 364-380) withdraws the offer locally and reports `unavailable`/`alreadyClaimed`, so the UI tells the driver the trip is gone while the server has assigned it to them.
failure_scenario: Flaky mobile network: POST /offers/{id}/accept commits on the server but the response times out -> app shows 'No connection', driver taps Match again -> new Idempotency-Key -> 409 -> island 'Trip no longer available' / 'Taken by another driver'; the trip never opens on this phone although dispatch locked it to this driver.
evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:178-187 `Future<Map<String, String>> _headers({bool mutation = false}) async { ... if (mutation) 'Idempotency-Key': _key(), }`; :347-351 `response = await _client.post(_uri('/offers/.../accept'), headers: await _headers(mutation: true), body: jsonEncode({'expectedVersion': version}));`; :352-353 `} catch (_) { return const ClaimResult.networkError(); }`; driver_trip_gateway.dart:101-102 `/// 16–128 characters (contract.json#headers). Reuse it on retry.`
suggested_fix: Derive/keep one key per (offerId, body) attempt (e.g. store it in a map until a definitive 2xx/4xx arrives) and reuse it on the network-error retry; only mint a new key when the body changes (the version_mismatch retry).

title: The SSE offer feed subscription has no onError/onDone handling, so a dropped stream raises an unhandled error and the feed silently dies with no resync
description: connect() subscribes with `.listen((line) {...})` only. A transport error on the body stream (connection reset, TLS error) has no onError handler, so it is forwarded to the zone's uncaught-error handler, and onDone (server closed the stream) is ignored: `_feed` keeps pointing at a finished subscription, nothing reconnects from `lastSequence` or reloads `GET /driver/offers`, and the driver's offer list stays frozen with stale open offers. The contract's realtime rules require resync after gaps/disconnects. ApiDispatchRepository is not installed by the app today (class doc: 'nothing installs this class in the app'), so this is dormant.
failure_scenario: With the API dispatch adapter in use, the phone loses connectivity for a minute; the SSE stream errors. The error surfaces as an uncaught exception (debug) and the offer list never updates again until the app restarts; offers that were withdrawn server-side remain tappable and accept returns 404/409.
evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:255-271 `_feed = response.stream.transform(utf8.decoder).transform(const LineSplitter()).listen((line) { ... });` (no onError, no onDone, no reconnect)
suggested_fix: Pass onError/onDone to listen; on either, clear `_feed`, schedule a reconnect with backoff using `after=$_lastSequence`, and call `_load()` to resync the open-offer list.

title: Destination-mode demo offers carry English place phrases ('Pickup near you', 'On your way · 35 %', 'Away from your route', 'Behind you', 'Near …') shown on Radar cards in every language
description: `DemoDestinationTrips.along` (called from home_map_sheet.dart:445-450 whenever Destination mode is set) fills `pickup`/`dropoff` with English sentences, not addresses, and the default `destinationLabel: 'your destination'`. These are rendered as the pickup/drop-off lines of the Radar/Exclusive cards. The ARB already has `nearValue` ('Near {value}') and `onYourWay`, showing the intent to localize such copy.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver sets a destination: Radar shows cards whose pickup line reads 'Pickup near you' and drop-off 'On your way · 35 %' / 'Behind you' among Swedish labels.
evidence: demo_destination_trips.dart:24: `String destinationLabel = 'your destination',` :43: `pickup: 'Pickup near you',` :56-69: `'Near $destinationLabel'`, `'On your way · 35 %'`, `'On your way · 60 %'`, `'Away from your route'`, `'Behind you'` — home_map_sheet.dart:445-450: `final trips = DemoDestinationTrips.along( ... destinationLabel: _destinationShortLabel,`
suggested_fix: Build these labels from `tr` (nearValue, onYourWay, new keys) at seed time.

title: Pickup pay is folded into the fare shown on offer cards but never carried into the accepted trip, its snapshot, waybill or history
description: PickupPayQuote.totalOf(fare) returns fare + pickup pay and is what the cards display: the on-trip next-trip card shows `_NextTripRadarOffer.shownFare` (accept_ride.dart:333 `String get shownFare => pickupPay.totalOf(fare);`, rendered at accept_ride_panel.dart:309 and accept_ride_sheet.dart:132), the exclusive sheet shows `offer.shownFare(show)` and Home radar cards get a PickupPayQuote (home_offer_radar.dart:1069). PickupPayConfig.current defaults have every kind on with demo rates (pickup_pay_config.dart:188-209, demoRates), so for the default next-trip offer (Comfort, 1.6 km / 4 min: (1.6-1)*3 + (4-2)*1 = 3,80 kr) the card promises 132,20 kr. When the driver accepts, the trip is opened with the plain fare: _buildNextWaybill uses `offer.fare` (accept_ride_trip.dart:217), _snapshotForOffer uses `offer.fare` (:976), the next AcceptRide gets `fare: offer.fare` (:940, :1398), PersistedQueuedTrip.fare is the plain fare (:49), and Home's _openOfferTrip passes `fare: offer.fare` (home_offer_radar.dart:954). Nothing stores or adds the pickup pay afterwards, so the trip screen, completion journal, history and earnings all show the lower number the driver did not accept.
failure_scenario: While driving, the next-trip card says 132,20 kr (incl. 3,80 kr pickup) and the driver accepts. The secured-next banner, the next trip's screen, its waybill 'Your earnings' and the history row all say 128,40 kr; the 3,80 kr the card promised is gone. Same on Home radar/exclusive cards whenever pickup pay is non-zero.
evidence: pickup_pay.dart:38-44 `String totalOf(String fare) { if (!hasPay) { return fare; } final base = Money.parseSekLabel(fare); return base == null ? fare : (base + pay).formatted; }`  |  accept_ride.dart:333 `String get shownFare => pickupPay.totalOf(fare);`  |  accept_ride_panel.dart:309 `offer.shownFare,`  |  accept_ride_trip.dart:217 `fare: offer.fare,` (waybill) and :976 `fare: offer.fare,` (snapshot) and :940 `fare: offer.fare,` (AcceptRide)  |  home_offer_radar.dart:954 `fare: offer.fare,`
suggested_fix: Decide one truth: either carry the pickup pay into the trip (store it on the offer/snapshot/waybill and include it in earnings and the trip header), or show the card total as 'fare' plus a separate pickup-pay line that is clearly not part of the fare. At minimum pass `offer.shownFare` (or a stored PickupPayQuote) through _buildNextWaybill/_snapshotForOffer/_openOfferTrip so the accepted amount matches what was shown.

title: Demo document titles and demo notifications are localised once and cached, so they stay in the old language after the driver switches language
description: `DocumentExpiryStore.documents` lazily builds the demo list with `tr.docInsuranceLetter` etc. and caches it in `_documents` (line 110); only `load()`/`reset()` replace it and neither is called on a language change (`DriverLanguage.choose` → `_apply()` only flips `DriverAppTexts.language` and the notifier; no caller resets the store — grep shows no `DocumentExpiryStore.instance.reset()` in lib). The cached `title`/`shortTitle` feed the island and notification text (`home_account.dart:153-160` → `DriverNotices.documentExpiring(title: document.title, shortTitle: document.shortTitle)`), the Documents list (`documents.dart:224`) and the renewal sheet (`document_renewal.dart:65,168,304`). Reproduced with a throwaway test: with language `en` the first title is 'Insurance letter'; after setting the language to `sv` it is still 'Insurance letter' while `tr.docInsuranceLetter` is 'Försäkringsbrev'. The same pattern exists in `DriverNotificationFeed.items` (`driver_notifications.dart:127-128` caches `demoReceived`, whose first title is `tr.noticeNewScheduledRide` and whose bodies 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view', 'Bonus progress', 'Payout sent' are English literals even though a localised `tr.noticeScheduledBody` template exists).
failure_scenario: App starts in Swedish (zone default), the Home island already read the documents; the driver picks English in Settings. The island later says 'Försäkringsbrev expires in 7 days', the notification is 'Försäkringsbrev expires tomorrow' and the Documents screen keeps the Swedish names until the app is restarted. Conversely a Swedish driver always sees the three demo notifications in English.
evidence: document_expiry.dart:109-110 `List<TrackedDocument> get documents =>\n      List.unmodifiable(_documents ??= _seed ?? demo(_now()));` · document_expiry.dart:88-92 `title: tr.docInsuranceLetter, shortTitle: tr.insurance,` · driver_language.dart:105-109 `_apply()` only sets `DriverAppTexts.language`/`current.value` · driver_notifications.dart:127-128 `_items ??= DriverNotices.demoReceived(_now())` and :333 `body: 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view',` :341 `title: 'Bonus progress',` :347 `title: 'Payout sent',` · test output: `en title=Insurance letter, after switch to sv title=Insurance letter, tr now=Försäkringsbrev`
suggested_fix: Keep language-independent ids/keys in `TrackedDocument` and resolve the title through `tr` at read time (or rebuild the demo list when `DriverLanguage.current` changes); build the demo notifications with the existing `tr.noticeScheduledBody` and arb keys.

title: Cash balance direction labels ('You owe Movera', 'Movera owes you', 'Settled') are hard-coded English and shown in the French/Swedish UI
description: `CashBalance.direction()` returns English literals and `directionLabel` is rendered on the cash-collect sheet (`cash_collect_sheet.dart:294`) and in history detail (`history_detail.dart:432`), screens that are otherwise fully localised through `tr`. The arb files only contain `totalYouOweMovera` / `totalMoveraOwesYou` (app_en.arb:911-912, app_fr.arb:422-423); there is no key for these three short labels, so a Swedish or French driver (the zone default for Sweden is `sv`, see `DriverLanguage`) sees an English line on every cash trip.
failure_scenario: Driver app language is Svenska. A cash Premium reservation (fare 248,40 kr, cash 300,00 kr) is finished: the Collect-cash sheet and the trip's history detail show 'You owe Movera  −51,60 kr' in English between Swedish labels.
evidence:
cash_balance.dart:46-50 `static String direction(Money amount) => amount.minorUnits < 0
      ? 'You owe Movera'
      : amount.minorUnits > 0
      ? 'Movera owes you'
      : 'Settled';` · cash_collect_sheet.dart:294 `balance.directionLabel,` · history_detail.dart:432 `_detailRow(cash.directionLabel, cash.signedLabel)`
suggested_fix: Add `youOweMovera`, `moveraOwesYou`, `settled` keys to the arb files and return `tr.*` from `direction()` (or move the words to the presentation layer).

title: Distances and rates use a '.' decimal in fr/sv ('4.2 km', '2.4%') while the trip island localizes the decimal mark ('1,2 km'), so the same trip shows both forms
description: `driverDistanceMeters` formats with `toStringAsFixed` (dot) and is used on offer cards, reservation maps and scheduled rides; `navigation_instruction_banner.dart:331-333` does the same for the banner distance; `driver_home_admin_content.dart:74` (`cancellationLabel`) and acceptance_rate.dart:30 / cancelation_rate.dart:30 format percentages with a dot. `adaptive_trip_island.dart:519-521`, by contrast, replaces '.' with `tr.navDecimalMark` (',' in fr/sv). During navigation the island says '1,2 km' while the banner under it says '1.2 km'. Swedish and French conventions use the comma, as Money already does ('104,80 kr').
failure_scenario: Swedish driver on trip: island '1,2 km', navigation banner '1.2 km'; Radar card '4.2 km' beside a fare '104,80 kr'.
evidence: driver_distance.dart:9: `return '${km.toStringAsFixed(km < 9.95 ? 1 : 0)} km';` — navigation_instruction_banner.dart:333: `return '${km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0)} km';` — adaptive_trip_island.dart:520: `km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0).replaceAll('.', tr.navDecimalMark),` — driver_home_admin_content.dart:74: `String get cancellationLabel => '${cancellationRate.toStringAsFixed(1)}%';`
suggested_fix: Route all decimal formatting through one helper that applies `tr.navDecimalMark` (or NumberFormat with the driver locale).

title: Corrupt-record warnings log the raw stored JSON (rider names, addresses, free-text notes) through FormatException.toString()
description: `DriverLogRecord` documents that messages 'must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text' (driver_log.dart:5-6), and the default sink prints to the console in release builds too (`debugPrint`, driver_log.dart:42). Several readers interpolate the `FormatException` thrown by `jsonDecode` into the message. Dart's `FormatException.toString()` appends a window of the `source` string around the failing offset, so the log line carries whatever personal data sits near the corruption. Verified with a dart script: `jsonDecode` of a truncated history blob logged `...:"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm","phone":"+46701234567"` under 'History JSON malformed:'. Affected in-scope sites: history (`prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:88`, rider names/addresses), ride-check log (`ride_check_log.dart:104`, includes the driver's 'What happened' free text and answers), and settings (`settings_repository.dart:84` builds `reason: '$storageKey: $error'` which `local_quarantine.dart:62` logs; settings sections hold trusted-contact phone numbers and vehicle drafts). The same pattern exists in `prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:81` (out of scope) via `DriverLog.error(..., error, stack)` which the sink prints verbatim.
failure_scenario: A localStorage write is cut off mid-blob (web quota, process kill). On the next History open the console/crash log receives 'WARN History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character N) ..."riderName":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12...' — rider PII in a log that is meant to be shippable to a crash reporter.
suggested_fix: Log only `error.message` (and offset) for FormatException, never `$error`/`error.toString()`; in `DriverLog._debugSink` scrub `FormatException.source` before printing so no sink can leak stored blobs.

title: Island strip message '<stop> next' concatenates a hardcoded English word onto a localized stop label
description: TripStripController.update says `_say('${next.stopLabel} next')` when a stop leg starts. stopLabel comes from AdaptiveTripIsland.pointLabel (adaptive_trip_island.dart:271), which is `tr.stopNumber(_stopCursor + 1)` (accept_ride.dart:809) and is localized ('Arrêt 1' / 'Stopp 1' per app_fr.arb:27, app_sv.arb:27). Every other message in this controller goes through `tr.` (riderBags, trafficAheadValueMin, arrivingInEtaMinTimeTime2, nextTripSecuredNextTripFare, pickupOnPickupSideSide, tollAhead). There is no arb key for this string (grep of app_en.arb finds only holdToStopNextTrips / cancelReasonNextTripOtherDetail).
failure_scenario: A French- or Swedish-language driver on a multi-stop trip sees the island strip read 'Arrêt 1 next' / 'Stopp 1 next' when heading to a stop.
evidence: trip_island_controller.dart:321-323 `if (newLeg && next.leg == TripLeg.stop && next.stopLabel != null) { _say('${next.stopLabel} next'); }`  |  accept_ride.dart:809 `ArrivalPointKind.stop => tr.stopNumber(_stopCursor + 1),`  |  adaptive_trip_island.dart:271 `stopLabel: leg == TripLeg.stop ? widget.pointLabel : null,`
suggested_fix: Add an l10n key (e.g. `stopNext`: 'Stop {number} next' / 'Arrêt {number} ensuite' / 'Stopp {number} härnäst') and call `_say(tr.stopNext(...))`, or pass the already-localized full phrase in TripStripInput.

title: On web the GPS stream is gated behind a one-shot fix whose 8 s time limit is not enforced (geolocator_web passes microseconds as ms and applies no Dart timeout), so a slow or silent browser leaves the trip and Home without any GPS for hours
description: `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition()` relies on `LocationSettings(timeLimit: 8 s)` to bound the one-shot fix. Both screens subscribe to `watchPosition()` only after that call resolves: `accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606` (`final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(...)`) and `home_map_sheet.dart:38-45` (the catch path also subscribes, but only if the call completes). On native the platform-interface applies `.timeout(timeLimit)`, so after 8 s the service falls back to the last known fix or throws and the screens show `Location updating…` and keep working. On web the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 overrides `getCurrentPosition` with no Dart-side timeout and converts the limit with `timeout?.inMicroseconds` into the browser's millisecond `PositionOptions.timeout` (8 s becomes 8,000 s, about 2.2 h). The app's own guard therefore does not hold on its primary (web/PWA) deployment: when the browser's geolocation does not answer (device has location permission but no fix, e.g. indoors, or a slow provider), the one-shot neither resolves nor errors, no stream is ever subscribed, no `Location updating…` status is set, and on the trip no route request is made (`_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` sits in the catch).
failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA on a phone whose browser cannot obtain a fix right away: Home stays on the locating placeholder and the trip map shows no live car, no route and no status for as long as the browser withholds an answer (up to ~2.2 h) instead of falling back after 8 s as on native.
evidence: driver_location_service.dart:21-26: `LocationSettings get _settings => LocationSettings(accuracy: kIsWeb ? LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, timeLimit: const Duration(seconds: 8));` 29-36: `await _ensurePermission(); try { final position = await Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: _settings);`. accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606: `final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(`. geolocator_web-4.1.4 lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:34-37: `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds ?? const Duration(days: 1).inMilliseconds,`; geolocator_web.dart:74-85 awaits `_geolocation.getCurrentPosition(...)` with no `.timeout`.
suggested_fix: Wrap `Geolocator.getCurrentPosition` in a Dart-side `.timeout(_settings.timeLimit!)` in `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition` (and `requestPermission` if it can block), and/or subscribe to `watchPosition` before awaiting the one-shot so a hung one-shot cannot block the stream.

title: On web the last-known-position fallback throws UnsupportedError from inside the catch block, replacing the original GPS error and skipping the error log
description: `getCurrentPosition()` catches the live-fix error and calls `Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition()`. geolocator_web 4.1.4 implements that method as `throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition')` (geolocator_web.dart:68-71). The throw happens inside the `catch` clause, so it propagates out of the method before `vetCachedFix`, `DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack)` and `rethrow` run. Callers catch everything, so the screen outcome (`Location updating…`) is unchanged, but the diagnostic record of why GPS failed on web is lost and an unrelated `UnsupportedError` is what surfaces.
failure_scenario: On the PWA a timeout/permission error from the browser is reported as 'Unsupported operation: getLastKnownPosition is not supported on the web platform' with no 'No recent accurate GPS fix available' log, making field diagnosis of web GPS failures misleading.
evidence: driver_location_service.dart:37-49: `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.warn('Current GPS failed, trying last known: $error'); final last = await Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition(); ... DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack); rethrow; }`. geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart:68-71: `Future<Position> getLastKnownPosition({...}) { throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition'); }`.
suggested_fix: Skip the fallback on web (`if (kIsWeb) rethrow;`) or wrap `getLastKnownPosition()` in its own try/catch so the original error is logged and rethrown.

title: Trip auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is dropped and never re-armed; resume() does not reschedule it
description: `_scheduleResume()` arms a one-shot Timer whose callback returns early when `_suspended` is true without rescheduling, and `resume()` (lines 693-696) only calls `_request(immediate: true)`, which is a no-op in browsing mode (`_canFollow` is false). The trip screen relies on this timer to bring the camera back to the car 12 s after the driver lets go of the map (`accept_ride.dart:488` sets `autoResumeAfter = tripAutoResume`, `accept_ride_trip.dart:794` sets `onAutoResume`). `suspend()` is called from `_pauseLiveUpdates` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:117`) on every lifecycle pause. On Android and on the web (PWA tab in background) Dart timers keep firing while the app is hidden, so the 12 s timer runs during the pause, hits the `_suspended` guard and dies. After `resume()` nothing re-arms it: `mapActivity()` only reschedules when `_resumeTimer != null`, and a later `update()` only calls `_scheduleResume()` on `enteringGuidance`, which is false mid-trip. Reproduced with a throwaway Flutter test (controller with `autoResumeAfter` 50 ms: userGesture, touching=false, suspend, wait 120 ms, resume, wait 300 ms): `Expected: <1> Actual: <0> after resume the camera should still auto-return`, mode stayed `browsing`.
failure_scenario: Driver on an active trip pans the map (camera enters Free), switches to another app for more than 12 s on Android, comes back: the trip map stays where it was panned indefinitely; the camera never returns to the car until the driver touches the map again or taps recenter.
evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:472-484: `_resumeTimer = Timer(after, () { _resumeTimer = null; if (_disposed || _touching || _suspended || !isGuidance || mode != DriverCameraMode.browsing) { return; } ...`; 693-696: `void resume() { _suspended = false; _request(immediate: true); }`; 460-462: `void mapActivity() { if (_resumeTimer != null) _scheduleResume(); }`. Test run: `00:00 +0 -1: auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is never rescheduled [E] Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
suggested_fix: In the timer callback, when `_suspended` is true, leave `_resumeTimer` unset but have `resume()` call `_scheduleResume()` (it already checks mode/guidance/touching); alternatively cancel the timer in `suspend()` and re-arm it in `resume()`.

title: The 'same fix reported again' guard compares the route by identity, so every route refresh/reroute resolves the same GPS fix twice and doubles the per-fix zoom, speed and bearing smoothing steps
description: `update()` returns early only when `identical(location, _location) && identical(route, _route) && ...`. The trip calls `_camera.update(location, route: _navigation.route)` in `_applyDriverPosition` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:665`) and again from `_followVehicle()` after `_refreshRoadRoute()` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:731`). Whenever that refresh produced a new `RoadRoute` object (every 90 s silent refresh, every reroute, and `NavigationController.ensureRoute` always allocates a new `RoadRoute` at line 404), the second call passes the identity check and `DriverCameraPolicy.resolve` runs twice for one fix: `_smoothedSpeed` applies its 0.3 blend twice, `_cruiseZoom` may step up to 2×0.25 out / 2×0.4 in instead of once, and the bearing damping at lines 320-323 applies 0.65 of the remaining delta twice. The guard's own comment states the intent: 'Resolving it twice would smooth the turn twice.'
failure_scenario: During a reroute mid-turn the camera rotates and zooms with a visibly bigger single step than on other fixes (e.g. zoom 0.5 instead of 0.25 in one frame), the exact effect the guard was written to prevent.
evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557: `// The trip reports the same fix again once its route refresh is done. // Resolving it twice would smooth the turn twice. if (identical(location, _location) && identical(route, _route) && navigating == _navigating && waiting == _waiting) { return; }`. accept_ride_trip.dart:728-734: `Future<void> _followVehicle({bool force = false}) async { final location = _lastLocation; ... _camera.update(location: location, route: _navigation.route, ...`. navigation_controller.dart:404: `_route = RoadRoute(points: List<GeoPoint>.unmodifiable(route.points), ...`.
suggested_fix: When only the route changed for an already-resolved location, update the policy's route/geometry without re-running the speed, zoom and bearing smoothing (e.g. resolve with `immediate: false` but skip the smoothing when `identical(location, _location)`).

title: Demo notifications (bodies, two titles and an island popup) are hard-coded English and shown as-is on the Notifications screen and island in fr/sv
description: `DriverNotices.demoReceived` and `demoArrivals` build notices with English literals: body 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view', title 'Bonus progress' + body '18 of 25 trips this week. 7 more for 350 kr.', title 'Payout sent' + body '2 450,00 kr is on its way to your bank.', and the event arrival title 'Stockholm evening demand', body '18:00–22:30 · Central Stockholm. Be online before the main departure window.', island 'Event tonight · City'. `driver_notifications_screen.dart:256,280` renders `notice.title`/`notice.body` directly; the island shows `notice.island`. Other notices in the same file use `tr.*`, so this is an omission, not a design choice. In addition the list is cached once (`_items ??= DriverNotices.demoReceived(_now())`, line 134) so the localized parts keep the first language after a switch.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver opens Notiser: 'Ny bokad resa' followed by the English body 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view', then 'Bonus progress' and 'Payout sent' cards; 50 s after Home opens the island says 'Event tonight · City'.
evidence: driver_notifications.dart:333: `body: 'Tomorrow 07:40 · 126 kr · Tap to view',` — :341-342: `title: 'Bonus progress', body: '18 of 25 trips this week. 7 more for 350 kr.',` — :348-349: `title: 'Payout sent', body: '2 450,00 kr is on its way to your bank.',` — :362-365: `title: 'Stockholm evening demand', body: '18:00–22:30 · Central Stockholm. Be online before the ' 'main departure window.', island: 'Event tonight · City',` — driver_notifications_screen.dart:256: `notice.title,` :280: `notice.body,`
suggested_fix: Move these texts into the ARB (they are app demo content, not admin content) and build the list lazily per language.

title: DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse throws TypeError on a non-string `kind` although it is documented to skip broken envelopes
description: tryParse is the transport entry point ('X14: ... a broken envelope is skipped and returns null; it never stops the stream'). The kind check `DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?)` is executed outside the try block, so an envelope whose kind is not a String (e.g. a number or an object) throws TypeError from the cast instead of returning null; only exceptions raised inside fromJson are caught. No transport calls tryParse in lib yet (only test/core/realtime_unknown_kind_test.dart), so this is dormant until an SSE/WebSocket adapter uses it.
failure_scenario: A future adapter does `DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse(jsonDecode(frame))` on `{"kind": 7, ...}`; the call throws instead of returning null and, in a stream map/listen without onError, kills the subscription the contract expects to survive unknown envelopes.
evidence: driver_realtime.dart:147-162 `static DriverRealtimeEvent? tryParse(Object? json) { if (json is! Map) return null; final map = Map<String, dynamic>.from(json); if (DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?) == null) { return null; } try { return DriverRealtimeEvent.fromJson(map); } on FormatException { return null; } on TypeError { return null; } on ArgumentError { return null; } }`
suggested_fix: Read the kind defensively: `final kind = map['kind']; if (kind is! String || DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(kind) == null) return null;` or move the check inside the try.

title: applyProjection refuses while a background save is in flight instead of waiting (unlike every driver command), and its terminal caller does not retry after the journal step, leaving an authoritative terminal unapplied
description: D-09 (comment at lines 261-264) makes transitionTo/complete/cancel/noShow `await _afterBackgroundSave()` so a command that lands during a GPS/lifecycle persistNow waits instead of being dropped. applyProjection does not: `if (saving || _disposed || ...) return false;` (line 115). Its caller _drainProjection checks `_rideLifecycle.saving` only before the journal step (accept_ride_trip.dart:301-306, 100 ms retry); in the terminal branch it then `await`s CompletionJournal.finish (archive + markTerminal + handoff, :316) and only afterwards calls applyProjection (:319). If a persistNow started during that await (GPS snapshot every 2 min at :672-677, lifecycle pause at accept_ride.dart:724, secured-next at :1206), applyProjection returns false and _drainProjection returns without clearing _pendingProjection and without _scheduleProjectionRetry (no retry is scheduled in that branch). The trip is already archived and marked terminal on disk, but the controller is not terminal: subsequent Arrive/Start slides call transitionTo -> save, which throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:139) and the driver sees 'Trip progress could not be saved' with a Retry that also fails, until a Finish/Cancel tap reaches _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal.
failure_scenario: With a realtime transport delivering an authoritative cancelled_by_rider / cancelled_by_admin projection: the event arrives just as a throttled GPS snapshot save begins; the journal archives the trip, but the screen stays on the live trip, every Arrive/Start slide is rejected with a 'could not be saved' snackbar, and the outcome sheet only appears after the driver taps Finish or Cancel. Only reachable with a real transport (MemoryDriverRealtime is per-screen today).
evidence: active_ride_controller.dart:111-119 `Future<bool> applyProjection(TripStatus status) async { ... if (saving || _disposed || (terminal && (!status.isTerminal || _terminalStatus == status))) { return false; }`  vs :72-76 `Future<bool> transitionTo(ActiveRideStage next) async { if (_backgroundSave != null) { await _afterBackgroundSave(); } if (_disposed || terminal || saving) { return false; }`  |  accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(... authoritative:true, next:next); if (!mounted) { return; } if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; }` (no _scheduleProjectionRetry on this return)
suggested_fix: Have applyProjection `await _afterBackgroundSave()` like the driver commands before checking `saving`, and/or make _drainProjection call _scheduleProjectionRetry() whenever applyProjection returns false for a terminal/released status.

title: Corrupt local records leak rider/contact PII into the log channel via FormatException source excerpts
description: DriverLog's own contract (lib/core/logging/driver_log.dart:5-6: 'Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text') is violated by every storage reader that logs a jsonDecode error. Dart's FormatException.toString() appends ~78 characters of the offending source around the error offset, and the stored records are JSON blobs holding rider names, phone numbers and addresses (active ride), trusted-contact phone numbers (settings sections) and completion journals. Paths: PrefsActiveRideRepository.read -> `DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack)` (line 81) and again through `_enqueue`'s catchError (line 57); LocalQuarantine.store builds `reason: '$error'` from callers (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:125, completion_journal.dart:157, settings_repository.dart:84) and then logs it: `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason')` (local_quarantine.dart:62). The default sink prints with debugPrint (driver_log.dart:42-43), which is not stripped in release builds, so this lands in logcat / the browser console; the file also says a crash-reporting adapter will be attached to this sink later. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: a truncated active-ride snapshot produced a log line containing `"riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`, and a truncated contacts section produced `"phone":"+46709998877"` in the quarantine warning.
failure_scenario: localStorage/SharedPreferences holds a half-written movera_driver_active_ride (e.g. tab killed mid-write) -> next launch Home calls read() -> the rider's name, phone and pickup address are printed to the device/browser log in a release build and would be shipped to any future crash-reporting sink.
evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:80-82 `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack); throw ActiveRideUnreadable(error); }`; local_quarantine.dart:62 `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason');`; settings_repository.dart:84 `reason: '$storageKey: $error',`; driver_log.dart:5-6 `/// Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text; trip IDs and status names are allowed.`; test output: `Active-ride snapshot parse failed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character 123)\n...na Svensson","riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`
suggested_fix: Log only the exception type/message without the source excerpt (e.g. `error is FormatException ? error.message : error.runtimeType`), and pass a scrubbed `reason` to LocalQuarantine (the raw text is already stored in the quarantine payload, so the reason need not repeat it).

title: clearForTrip/save/handoff call jsonDecode on the raw snapshot without tolerating an undecodable value, so a corrupt snapshot makes the completion journal unrepayable and Home recovery permanently fails
description: read() and quarantineUnreadable() go through _decodeSnapshot and convert a decode failure into ActiveRideUnreadable (lines 77-83, 117-127), matching LOCAL_DATA.md ("A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers"). The three writers do not: clearForTrip (line 290 `final data = jsonDecode(raw);`), save (line 143) and handoff (line 168) let a FormatException from invalid JSON propagate (save also does `ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String)` at 151, which throws on a valid-JSON map with a bad stage). CompletionJournal._replay runs history.archive -> markTerminal -> clearForTrip(id) (completion_journal.dart:259) with no guard, so the thrown FormatException leaves the journal in prefs and makes finish() throw; every retry replays the same journal and fails at the same step. On the next Home, _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded awaits CompletionJournal.reconcile() BEFORE repo.read() (home.dart:508-514); reconcile throws the FormatException, which is caught by the generic `catch (_)` (home.dart:519) and shown as recoveryFailed, so the ActiveRideUnreadable path that offers 'Close unreadable trip' (home.dart:515-517) is never reached, _recoveryResolved stays false and the driver cannot go online (home.dart:335). Only logout (clearLocalUserData) clears it. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: prefs key set to '{not json'; read() -> ActiveRideUnreadable (handled), clearForTrip('T1') -> FormatException, CompletionJournal.finish(...) -> FormatException with the journal left in prefs, reconcile() -> FormatException.
failure_scenario: The movera_driver_active_ride value becomes undecodable mid-trip (truncated localStorage write on the PWA, storage corruption). The driver taps Finish: the trip is archived to history and marked terminal, then clearForTrip throws -> 'Could not finish saving this trip'; every retry fails the same way and the driver cannot leave the trip. After a restart, Home shows 'saved trip could not be opened' on every launch, never offers the unreadable-trip closure dialog, and the driver cannot go online until they log out.
evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:283-297 `Future<void> clearForTrip(String tripId) => _enqueue(() async { ... final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw == null) { return; } final data = jsonDecode(raw); if (data is! Map || data['tripId'] != tripId) { return; } ...`  |  :141-151 `final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw != null) { final current = jsonDecode(raw); ... final stage = ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String);`  |  completion_journal.dart:258-259 `if (repository is TerminalRideRepository) { await (repository as TerminalRideRepository).clearForTrip(id); }` (no try/catch; journal removed only afterwards at :268)  |  home.dart:508 `final journal = await CompletionJournal(active: repo).reconcile();` precedes :514 `snapshot = await repo.read();`  |  test output: `clearForTrip() -> FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 2)` / `finish() -> FormatException; journal left = true` / `reconcile() -> FormatException`
suggested_fix: In clearForTrip/save/handoff decode the raw value with a guarded helper (try jsonDecode, treat non-Map/invalid JSON as 'not owned by any trip'); for clearForTrip that means returning without error, for save/handoff it means treating the slot as free (or quarantining it first). Alternatively have Home call repo.read() (or a cheap decode probe) before reconcile() so ActiveRideUnreadable is surfaced and the closure dialog still appears.

title: formatDistance shows '1000 m' for distances between 999.5 m and 1000 m instead of '1.0 km'
description: The branch chooses the metre format on the raw value (`meters < 1000`) but prints `meters.round()`, so 999.5..999.99 rounds up to 1000 and is rendered as `1000 m`, while 1000.0 renders as `1.0 km`. This is the live banner distance (`navigation_controller.dart:593` `distanceLabel: RouteInstructionCopy.formatDistance(meters)`), fed every fix with continuous metres from `RouteProgressCalculator`.
failure_scenario: Island reads 'Turn left in 1000 m' for one or more fixes just before switching to '1.0 km'/'999 m', an inconsistent unit boundary visible to the driver.
evidence: route_instruction.dart:536-545: `if (meters < nowMeters) { return l.navDistanceNow; } if (meters < 1000) { return l.navMeters('${meters.round()}'); } final km = meters / 1000; return l.navKilometers(km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0)...`
suggested_fix: Round first (`final rounded = meters.round();`) and branch on the rounded value, or use `meters < 999.5`.

title: Ride-check audio that is still starting when the card closes keeps the microphone recording with no UI, and dispose() never stops it after a later check opens
description: `toggleRecording()` sets `_audio = starting`, awaits `recorder.requestPermission()` and then `recorder.start(...)` (lines 240-251). On native that start awaits `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, `Directory.create` and the plugin. If the driver answers meanwhile (`imOk`/`done` → `_close()`), `_close()` calls `_stopRecording()` which returns immediately because `_audio != recording` (line 275), then marks the record answered and closes the card. When `start()` later completes, the only guard is `if (_disposed)` (line 260): `_audio` becomes `recording`, `_audioStartedAt` is set and a periodic 1 s ticker starts notifying listeners (lines 264-270) although the card is closed and `_answerable` is false, so nothing on screen shows a recording and no button can stop it. If a further Ride check opens later, `open()` resets `_audio = idle` (line 114) without touching the recorder or the ticker, after which `dispose()` skips the stop because `_audio != recording` (line 412) — the native recorder is never stopped for the rest of the process. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test using a recorder whose `start()` awaits a Completer: after `imOk()` and completing start, `c.audio == RideCheckAudio.recording` and the fake recorder was still recording; after `open()` of a second event and `dispose()`, the recorder was still recording with `stops == 0` (test output: `after close: audio=RideCheckAudio.recording recorderRecording=true stops=0` / `after dispose: recorderRecording=true stops=0`). The test file was deleted afterwards.
failure_scenario: Long-stop card opens, driver taps 'Record audio' and, while the OS mic permission sheet / recorder start is still in flight (hundreds of ms on a phone), taps 'I'm OK'. The card closes but the phone keeps recording the cabin to ride_check_audio/*.m4a with no indicator; after the next Ride check on the same trip and leaving the trip screen, the recorder is still running until the app process dies.
evidence: ride_check_controller.dart:250-251 `if (_disposed || !_answerable) return;\n      await recorder.start(...)` · :260-265 `if (_disposed) { unawaited(recorder.cancel()); return; }\n    _audio = RideCheckAudio.recording;` (no `_answerable`/`_closing` check after the await) · :273-275 `Future<void> _stopRecording() async { final recorder = _recorder; if (recorder == null || _audio != RideCheckAudio.recording) return;` · :114 `_audio = RideCheckAudio.idle;` in `open()` · :412-415 `if (_audio == RideCheckAudio.recording) { unawaited(_recorder?.stop()...` in `dispose()`
suggested_fix: After `await recorder.start(...)` re-check `_disposed || _closing || !_answerable` and cancel/stop the recorder if the card is no longer open; in `open()` and `dispose()` stop any recorder that was started regardless of the `_audio` flag (track a `_recorderRunning` bool set around start/stop).

title: Ride-check recordings are written to the iOS Documents directory, which is included in iCloud/iTunes backups, contradicting the 'saved only on this phone' permission text
description: `start()` saves audio under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio`. On iOS that is `NSDocumentDirectory`, which Apple backs up to iCloud/Finder by default unless the file is flagged `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` or stored under Application Support/Caches. `ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10` tells the user 'The recording is saved only on this phone' and `safety_alert_repository.dart:36` repeats 'recordings stay on the phone'. Cabin audio of riders therefore leaves the device whenever the driver has iCloud backup on, which the stated promise and GDPR expectations do not cover.
failure_scenario: Driver with iCloud Backup enabled records a Ride check conversation with a rider; the .m4a is uploaded to Apple's servers with the next device backup although the app told the driver it stays only on the phone.
evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-33 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio');` · ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10 `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` … 'The recording is saved only on this phone.'
suggested_fix: Store recordings under `getApplicationSupportDirectory()` and mark the folder excluded from backup (or set `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` on each file).

title: NativeRideCheckRecorder leaks: a zero-byte recording file is left on disk and the AudioRecorder is never disposed
description: `stop()` returns null for an empty capture but does not delete the file it just created in `ride_check_audio/` (line 48), so every failed/instant stop leaves an orphan `.m4a` under the app documents folder; nothing in the app ever lists or prunes that directory. Separately, `AudioRecorder` (record 7.1.1 exposes `Future<void> dispose()`, record.dart:173) is created per `RideCheckController` via `services.createRecorder()` (ride_check_controller.dart:234) and neither `NativeRideCheckRecorder` nor `RideCheckController.dispose()` releases it, so each trip in which the driver taps Record leaves a native recorder instance (method-channel/stream subscription) alive.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Record then immediately Stop on several trips: each leaves an empty `ride-check-<trip>-<ms>.m4a` in Documents/ride_check_audio (grows forever) and one undisposed native recorder per trip for the life of the process.
evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:47-48 `final file = File(path);\n    if (!await file.exists() || await file.length() == 0) return null;` (no delete) · ride_check_recorder_native.dart:15-56 has no `dispose` · ride_check_controller.dart:406-423 `dispose()` never disposes `_recorder` · record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:173 `Future<void> dispose()`
suggested_fix: Delete the empty file before returning null; add `dispose()` to `RideCheckRecorder` that calls `AudioRecorder.dispose()` and invoke it from `RideCheckController.dispose()`.

title: Saved Ride-preferences category choice is never restored at boot, so switched-off categories are offered again after every restart
description: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` (ride_categories.dart:56) is the in-memory set that every offer filter reads (`DriverCategoryChoice.takes` in home_offer_rules.dart:13/21/30, home_reservation.dart:107/132, scheduled_rides.dart:545). The only writer is the Ride preferences screen: `_publishChoice()` runs after `_restoreSettings()` or a toggle (preferences.dart:118/172), i.e. only once that screen has been opened. The choice is persisted to the `categories` settings section (preferences.dart:140), but nothing reads it back at app start: `main.dart:41-49` restores `MapTrafficSetting` and `DriverLanguage` and nothing else, and `DriverCategoryChoice` has no restore method. After a cold start `off` is the empty const set, so `takes()` returns true for every allowed category. The class comment (`ride_categories.dart:51`, 'kept for the session') documents the in-memory nature but the persisted setting and the Q27 promise ('offers follow that choice') make the restart behaviour wrong. The same global is also not reset on logout (`main.dart:180-195` calls `MapTrafficSetting.reset()` / `DriverLanguage.reset()` but not `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`), so after logout the cleared storage and the stale in-memory set disagree until Preferences is opened again.
failure_scenario: Driver opens Ride preferences, switches off 'Movera Pet' (saved to settings), kills and relaunches the app, goes online. Home shows Radar/Exclusive/reservation offers in the Pet category (and scheduled Pet rides) because `DriverCategoryChoice.off` is empty; the filter only starts working again after the driver happens to open Ride preferences.
evidence: ride_categories.dart:56-57 `static final ValueNotifier<Set<String>> off = ValueNotifier<Set<String>>(const <String>{});` · ride_categories.dart:61-63 `static bool takes(String category) => DriverCategoryAccess.current.allows(category) && !off.value.contains(...)` · preferences.dart:172 `DriverCategoryChoice.off.value = {` (only writer, after `_restoreSettings` at :118) · main.dart:41 `unawaited(MapTrafficSetting.restore());` main.dart:46 `await DriverLanguage.restore()...` (no categories restore) · main.dart:185-186 `MapTrafficSetting.reset(); DriverLanguage.reset();` (no `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`)
suggested_fix: Add `DriverCategoryChoice.restore([SettingsRepository])` that reads the `categories` section the same way `_restoreSettings` does and publishes the off-set; call it from `main()` beside `MapTrafficSetting.restore()`, and call `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()` in `_logout`.

title: WaybillPayment.fromFare reads only the first digit group of a thousands-grouped fare label, so earnings/fee are wrong for fares >= 1 000 kr
description: Money.formatted groups thousands with a space ("1 234,50 kr", lib/core/money/money.dart:187 via _group). RideOffer.fareLabel (dispatch_repository.dart:114) and WaitingTerms.addFee (waiting_rules.dart:77, used for _fareWithWaiting on completion) both produce this format, and it is what reaches WaybillRecord.fare. WaybillPayment.fromFare parses the label with `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare)` which matches only the leading "1" of "1 234,50 kr", so fareOre becomes 100 and _comma is false. Consumers: waybill_sheet.dart:70 (`WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)` -> "Your earnings" row) and OfferCardDetails.fare (offer_rules.dart:157, the net-fare mode admin can switch on for offer cards). Money.parseSekLabel already accepts the grouped form (money.dart:73), so the producer and this consumer disagree. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: `Money(minorUnits:123450).formatted` = "1 234,50 kr"; `WaybillPayment.fromFare(that)` gave fare=1.00 kr, fee=0.25 kr, earnings=0.75 kr; `OfferCardDetails(netFare:true).fare(label)` = "0.75 kr".
failure_scenario: A driver completes a 1 234,50 kr trip (any backend Offer.fare >= 100000 minor units, or a demo fare pushed over 1 000 kr by waiting fees). Opening the waybill shows "Your earnings 0.75 kr" and "Service fee 0.25 kr" instead of about 925,88 kr / 308,62 kr; with netFare on, the offer card shows a 0.75 kr net fare for a 1 234 kr trip.
evidence: waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);` ... :301 `final fareOre = (value * 100).round();`  |  money.dart:187 `return '$sign${_group(int.parse(parts[0]))},${parts[1]} $symbol';` (groups thousands with a space)  |  waybill_sheet.dart:70 `final payment = WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus);`  |  test output: `formatted = "1 234,50 kr"` / `fare=1.00 kr fee=0.25 kr earnings=0.75 kr` / `netFare card = 0.75 kr` / `parseSekLabel = 123450`
suggested_fix: Parse the fare with Money.parseLabel/parseSekLabel (which understand grouped thousands and the currency suffix) instead of the ad-hoc regex, e.g. `final money = Money.parseLabel(fare); if (money == null) return null; fareOre = money.minorUnits;` and keep the comma flag from the label. Add a test for a >= 1 000 kr label.

title: French plurals use =1/other so zero renders as plural ('0 courses', '0 arrêts', 'dans 0 jours')
description: French grammar uses the singular for 0 and 1 (CLDR 'one' covers 0 and 1 for fr). The ARB strings tripsCount (713), stopsCount (714), riderBags (676), inDaysCount (861), schedRidesHidden (904) and ratingAndRides (1319) are written as `{count, plural, =1{...} other{...}}`, so count 0 selects the 'other' branch and the UI shows '0 courses', '0 arrêts', 'Le passager a 0 bagages', 'dans 0 jours', '0 courses masquées'. The gen-l10n plural rules would do the right thing if the `one` category were used instead of `=1`. The English and Swedish files are fine with =1/other.
failure_scenario: French driver opens history with no rides or a reservation with zero stops; the counters read '0 courses' / '0 arrêts' instead of '0 course' / '0 arrêt'.
evidence: lib/l10n/app_fr.arb:713 `"tripsCount": "{count, plural, =1{1 course} other{{count} courses}}"`; :714 stopsCount; :676 riderBags; :861 inDaysCount; :904 schedRidesHidden; :1319 ratingAndRides
suggested_fix: In app_fr.arb use `one{...}` (CLDR category) instead of `=1{...}` for these keys, or add `=0{0 course}` branches.

title: A failed clearLocalUserData leaves the driver logged in with every long-lived storage repository invalidated (generation already bumped) and no recovery
description: `clearLocalUserData()` calls `LocalWriteSession.beginCleanup()` (local_data.dart:114), which increments the generation before any key is removed; every repository instance created earlier (`_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` in main.dart:93, the settings/vehicle stores held by open screens) now fails `LocalWriteSession.check` with 'Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving'. If a `prefs.remove` returns false the function throws (local_data.dart:135-137/148-150), `_logout` rethrows before reaching `_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` (main.dart:187) and `_session.reset()`, and Profile just shows 'could not clear' and keeps the driver signed in (profile.dart:397-406). From then on active-ride snapshots and terminal markers can no longer be written (every enqueued op logs 'Active-ride storage operation failed'), so crash recovery of a trip silently stops working, and local data is half-cleared, until the process restarts.
failure_scenario: On a device where SharedPreferences commit fails for one key (full disk, broken prefs file), the driver taps Log out, sees 'Could not clear local data', continues driving; the next accepted trip is not persisted, so a crash mid-trip comes back to an empty Home.
suggested_fix: Recreate the composition-root repositories (and reset the session) in a `finally`, or bump the generation only after the removals succeeded / roll it back on failure.

title: Crash/reload restore drops pickupKm, so the far-pickup waiting rule disappears and the waiting fee / no-show terms change mid-trip
description: `_waitTerms` is computed from `widget.pickupKm` (accept_ride.dart:989-996). Home passes the offer's `pickupKm` (home_offer_radar.dart:974) so a pickup over `farPickupKm` (5 km) gets the 'Pickup far away' rule: 1 free minute and an 85 kr no-show fee instead of 5 free minutes / 65 kr (waiting_rules.dart). `PersistedActiveRide` has no pickupKm field, `_buildSnapshot` (accept_ride_trip.dart:8-62) does not store it, and `AcceptRide.fromPersisted` (accept_ride.dart:240-292) never passes it, so after the documented crash/reload/PWA restore (`Home restores AcceptRide.fromPersisted`) the trip runs with the base terms. The pickup wait that was paid from minute 1 before the restore is now free until minute 5 (`_inIncludedWait`, `_paidWaitNow` = `_waitSeconds - 300`), the no-show option appears later, and the fee the trip earns (`_paidWaybill`, `_cashToCollect`) is lower than the terms shown before the restore. `WaitingTerms.active` and the waiting sheet also lose the 'Rule for this pickup' line. (`bags` and `offerId` are lost the same way; cosmetic.)
failure_scenario: Driver accepts a 7 km pickup (far-pickup rule), arrives, waits 3 minutes: 2 paid minutes shown. The PWA reloads; the restored screen now shows 'included wait' until 5 min, the no-show button is gone until 5 min, and the final waiting fee/cash to collect is computed with 5 free minutes.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart:989-996 `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(
    category: widget.category,
    type: ..., pickupKm: widget.pickupKm,
  );` ; fromPersisted 253-291 passes no `pickupKm`; active_ride_repository.dart PersistedActiveRide fields contain no pickupKm; waiting_rules.dart `if (pickupKm != null && pickupKm > farPickupKm) { ... terms._with(farPickup ...) }`
suggested_fix: Persist `pickupKm` (and `bags`) in `PersistedActiveRide`/`_buildSnapshot` and pass it in `AcceptRide.fromPersisted`; alternatively persist the resolved `WaitingTerms`.

title: Disposing the trip screen while a Ride check is open flips RideCheckGate synchronously and makes Home call setState while the widget tree is locked
description: `_AcceptRideState.dispose` calls `_rideCheck.dispose()` (679). `RideCheckController.dispose` calls `_syncGate(false)` (ride_check_controller.dart 409), which, when the gate was held (a Ride check pill/card was open), sets `RideCheckGate.set(false)` → `ValueNotifier` notifies synchronously. Home is still mounted underneath and its listener `_rideCheckGateListener` → `_onRideCheckGate` (home_offer_radar.dart 473-478) runs `_rebuild(() {})`, i.e. `setState` (home.dart 338), from inside another State's `dispose`. State.dispose runs in `BuildOwner.finalizeTree` under `lockState`, where `markNeedsBuild` asserts "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked". In debug/profile builds the FlutterError is thrown out of `_rideCheck.dispose()`, so the remainder of `AcceptRide.dispose` (camera, realtime subscription/unsubscribe, timers, animation controllers at 680-700+) never runs, leaking the realtime subscription, the 20 s ride-check ticker already cancelled but `_waitTimer`, `_nextTrip*` timers and the two AnimationControllers (which then also report "disposed with an active Ticker"). Release builds only mark Home dirty and rebuild.
failure_scenario: A Ride check card is open (long stop / off-route) when the rider cancels (or admin releases the trip); the trip screen pops. In a debug or profile build the framework reports "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked" during finalizeTree and AcceptRide's dispose is cut short, leaving its realtime subscription and timers alive.
evidence:
accept_ride.dart 675-679: `void dispose() { RideCheckGate.listenable.removeListener(_onRideCheckGateListener); ... _rideCheck.dispose();`
ride_check_controller.dart 407-409: `void dispose() { _disposed = true; _syncGate(false);` and 400-404: `if (open == _holdsGate) return; _holdsGate = open; RideCheckGate.set(open);`
home_offer_radar.dart 473-475: `void _onRideCheckGate() { if (!mounted || RideCheckGate.open) { return; } _rebuild(() {});`
home.dart 338: `void _rebuild(VoidCallback update) => setState(update);`
suggested_fix: Close the gate before the route is popped (e.g. in `_pauseLiveUpdates`/the exit paths) or defer the Home reaction with `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback`/`scheduleMicrotask` in `_onRideCheckGate`; alternatively have `RideCheckController.dispose` schedule `RideCheckGate.set(false)` asynchronously.

title: An authoritative `completed` projection archives a cash trip without its payment method, cash collected or waiting fee
description: The driver's own Finish (`_completeCurrentTrip`, lines 912-917) journals `_paidWaybill()` (fare incl. the driver's waiting fee) with `paymentMethod: 'Cash'` and `cashCollected` for a cash trip; `TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance` and the history 'Other earnings' cash accounting depend on `paymentMethod == 'cash'`. The realtime terminal path in `_drainProjection` (contract rows `complete` by admin from rider_onboard/in_trip/approaching_dropoff, or a server echo of `completed`) journals `_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill()` with only `status` and `authoritative: true`. The archived row then has no `paymentMethod`/`cashCollected` and no waiting fee, so the driver's cash balance for that trip (what they owe or are owed) silently disappears from history, and with `authoritative: true` it also overwrites a correct local row if one was written first.
failure_scenario: Cash trip in progress; admin force-completes it (`POST /admin/trips/{id}/complete`) -> `trip_projection` status completed arrives -> history row shows the trip as card-paid with no 'Cash collected' line; the period's cash balance sheet omits it.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:316-317 `await CompletionJournal(active: ...).finish(_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill(), status: status, authoritative:true, next:next);` vs :914-917 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(paid, next: next, paymentMethod: widget.paidByCash ? 'Cash' : null, cashCollected: widget.paidByCash ? _cashToCollect : null);`; trip_history.dart:59 `bool get paidByCash => paymentMethod.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash';`
suggested_fix: In the authoritative terminal branch pass the same `paymentMethod`/`cashCollected` (and `_paidWaybill()`) as the local completion when `status == TripStatus.completed`.

title: A repeated same-stage projection re-runs the stage side effects: an accepted next trip is dropped, a shown offer vanishes and the ride-check detector restarts
description: `_drainProjection` treats a successful `applyProjection` as a stage change: `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); _resumeStageSideEffects(); }` (lines 340-342). But `ActiveRideController.applyProjection` returns true without changing anything when `next == _stage` (active_ride_controller.dart: 'Realtime may repeat the same stage each poll ... if (next == _stage) { return true; }'). Same-stage projections are normal: `reconnectAndResync` (called on every app resume, accept_ride.dart:719, and on every sequence gap, accept_ride_trip.dart:248) re-emits the cached projection with a new sequence (driver_realtime.dart:468-482), and a poll/echo would do the same. For `onTrip`, `_resumeStageSideEffects` (100-115) then calls `_rideCheckDetector.startTrip(...)` (forgetting any long-stop/off-route progress), `_demoDrive?.startTrip()`, `_startOnTripRadar()` (995-1008) which cancels `_nextTripRadarMatchTimer` and sets `scanning` with `_nextTripRadarOffer = null` — so an offer the driver has just accepted (900 ms `matching` window, 1190-1208) is silently discarded after `ExclusiveAnswers.accepted()` was already counted, and an offer on screen disappears — and finally `_refreshOnTripRoute(fitCamera: true)` forces a route re-fetch and camera re-follow. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: on-trip demo offer shown, tap 'match next', emit an `in_trip` projection: `securedCardPresent=false offerVisible=true` (the same offer is re-presented as a new one instead of being secured).
failure_scenario: Driver on trip accepts the Exclusive next-trip offer; within a second the app is resumed or a projection echo arrives with status in_trip. The match timer is cancelled, the state goes back to scanning, the accepted trip is lost and the same offer pops up again (or is gone if declined before); the long-stop ride-check timer also restarts from zero.
suggested_fix: Only run `_resumeStageSideEffects()` when the stage actually changed (compare `_stage` before/after `applyProjection`, or have `applyProjection` report 'unchanged' distinctly), and make `_startOnTripRadar` a no-op when state is `matching`/`offerAvailable`.

title: An authoritative `completed` projection discards the waybill instead of completing it and journals the trip without payment method, cash collected or waiting fee
description: `_drainProjection` handles every terminal status through `_leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome` (313-323 → 371-390). For `TripStatus.completed` that path writes the journal with the bare current waybill (`_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill()`, no `paymentMethod`, no `cashCollected`, no `_paidWaybill()` waiting fee — unlike `_completeCurrentTrip` at 912-917) and then calls `_waybills.discardCurrent()` (376) rather than `completeCurrent()`. `discardCurrent` only nulls `current` (waybill.dart:195-197) so `_waybills.last` is never updated; Home's `lastListenable` listener (`_onLastTripChanged`, `_lastTripFareLabel`, `_lastTripSettling`) and the island 'Last trip' amount keep the previous trip, and a cash trip completed by the backend is archived without 'Cash'/cash collected, so the history detail cannot show what is owed to Movera (Q23).
failure_scenario: Backend/admin marks the trip completed while the driver is on the last leg. The outcome sheet says 'Movera recorded this trip as completed', but the Home island still shows the previous trip as last trip and the history entry for this cash trip has no payment method or cash collected.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:316-317 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(\n            _waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill(), status: status, authoritative:true, next:next);` ; 376 `_waybills.discardCurrent();` ; waybill.dart:195-197 `void discardCurrent() { _current.value = null; }` vs 183-191 completeCurrent sets `_last`
suggested_fix: Branch on `status == TripStatus.completed`: journal with `_paidWaybill()`, `paymentMethod`/`cashCollected` as in `_completeCurrentTrip`, and call `_waybills.completeCurrent()` (or route to DriverRideCompleted).

title: Terminal exits call Navigator.pop() on whatever route is on top, so a rider cancel (or any authoritative outcome) while Chat/Preferences/a modal sheet is open leaves the dead trip screen mounted
description: Every authoritative exit from the trip screen ends with a plain pop of the navigator: `_handleRiderCancelled` (lines 452-458 `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { IslandMessages.show(...); ... home.pop(); return; }` and 478-481), `_leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome` (388-389), `_leaveAfterRelease` (403-407) and `_submitTripCancellation` (1444-1446). `Navigator.pop()` removes the topmost route, not the AcceptRide route. The trip screen itself pushes other routes onto the same navigator while the trip is live: `_messageRider` pushes `Chat` (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867), `_openRidePreferences` pushes `Preferences` (536-541), `_openDestinationPicker` pushes the picker, the island pushes `DriverRideHistory` (accept_ride.dart:1307-1308), plus modal sheets (trip options, rider profile, cash collect, waiting time, safety toolkit, the accessible-confirm AlertDialog). A realtime `rider_cancelled`/terminal/`searching` event arriving while any of those is on top therefore pops that page instead of the trip: `_handleRiderCancelled` has already journaled the cancel, set the lifecycle terminal, run `_pauseLiveUpdates()` (GPS off, wait timer off), `_waybills.discardCurrent()` and queued an island notice for a Home that is never shown.
