The driver is left on a terminal AcceptRide: the slide/arrive actions return silently (`_advanceRide` checks `_rideLifecycle.terminal`), cancel says it cannot be cancelled, `PopScope(canPop:false)` blocks Back. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Home -> AcceptRide waiting -> a page pushed on top -> `realtime.emit(riderCancelled)`): result `chatPopped=true tripStillMounted=true homeVisible=false island=Rider cancelled`. Rider cancelling while the driver is in the chat with that rider is a very plausible sequence.
failure_scenario: Driver is waiting at pickup, opens Message rider (Chat page on top). The rider cancels; realtime delivers rider_cancelled. The Chat page closes, the trip screen stays with GPS stopped and the waybill discarded; nothing on it works any more and Back is blocked. The 'Rider cancelled' island notice is queued for Home, which is not reached.
suggested_fix: Pop to the trip's own route instead of the top route: capture `ModalRoute.of(context)` in the trip state and use `navigator.popUntil((r) => r != tripRoute && !r.isCurrent ...)` / `removeRoute`-style exit (e.g. `Navigator.of(context).popUntil((route) => route.isFirst)` when Home is the root, or `navigator.removeRoute(tripRoute)` after closing routes above it); for the `pushReplacement` branches first pop everything above the trip route.

title: Hard-coded English 'stop'/'pickup' is injected into the localized 'move within 100 m' message
description: `_blockedArrival` builds `final where = _stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip ? 'stop' : 'pickup';` and passes it to `tr.moveWithin100MOfWhere(where)`. The Swedish and French strings interpolate the raw word: `'Kom inom 100 m ($where) för att vara framme.'` / `'Approchez-vous à moins de 100 m ($where) ...'`, so Swedish and French drivers see 'Kom inom 100 m (pickup)'.
failure_scenario: App language Swedish; driver taps 'I've arrived' more than 100 m from the pickup: snackbar reads 'Kom inom 100 m (pickup) för att vara framme.'
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:503-506 `final where = _stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip ? 'stop' : 'pickup';
      ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(
        SnackBar(
          content: Text(tr.moveWithin100MOfWhere(where)),` ; app_localizations_sv.dart:457 `return 'Kom inom 100 m ($where) för att vara framme.';`
suggested_fix: Pass localized words (`tr.stop` / `tr.pickup`) or two separate localized messages.

title: Route-cleared notification is dropped while _stageTransitioning, so the pickup route line and ETA stay drawn through the whole wait at pickup
description: `_confirmPickupArrival` sets `_stageTransitioning = true` (541) and awaits `transitionTo(waitingForRider)`; the controller's commit notifies `_syncNavigationStage` → `NavigationController.setStage` which clears `_route` and notifies (navigation_controller.dart:163-188). `_onNavigationChanged` returns at once because `_stageTransitioning` is still true (562), so `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` keep the pickup route; the following `_rebuild(() {})` (558) calls `_syncRouteLines()` which redraws that stale route. During waiting `ensureRoute` returns early and `setVehicle` does not notify while the car is parked (moved < 0.4 m, navigation_controller.dart:242-246), so nothing clears it until the car moves. `_routeEtaText` likewise keeps the old duration (`routeFraction` is null → full duration) while waiting.
failure_scenario: Driver taps 'I've arrived' at the pickup. The waiting stage starts but the black route line to the pickup (and the old ETA value) remain on the map for the whole wait.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:561-562 `void _onNavigationChanged() {\n      if (!mounted || _stageTransitioning) { return; }` ; 547-559 `_waitSeconds = 0; ... if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); }\n      _unlockStageAfterFrame();` ; navigation_controller.dart:168 `_route = null;` inside setStage
suggested_fix: Do not skip `_onNavigationChanged` during a stage transition (or re-run it in `_unlockStageAfterFrame`), and clear `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` explicitly when entering waiting.

title: DECISIONS.md records a 20 m web GPS filter for the active ride, but the code subscribes with distanceFilter 0 on every platform
description: DECISIONS.md ('Active ride crash recovery (Safari / PWA)', line 85) states the Safari tab-kill fix included 'web GPS filter is 20m'. The active ride subscribes with `watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)` and DriverLocationService._streamSettings builds `LocationSettings(accuracy: high, distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters)` for web, so on web every browser geolocation callback (typically ~1 Hz, more on some devices) reaches _applyDriverPosition. There is no kIsWeb branch anywhere in accept_ride*.dart (grep shows none) and no constant 20 in the location code. The documented decision and the shipped behaviour differ; the task rules treat that as a defect to report.
failure_scenario: Safari PWA on an active trip: each raw geolocation fix (no distance gating) drives _applyDriverPosition, route-refresh checks and island updates, the very load pattern the recorded decision says was limited by a 20 m filter.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:85 `GPS setState is gone; web GPS filter is 20m.`; accept_ride_trip.dart:604-606 `_positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0)`; driver_location_service.dart:58-67 `if (kIsWeb || !navigation) { return LocationSettings(accuracy: kIsWeb ? LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters); }`
suggested_fix: Either pass `distanceFilterMeters: kIsWeb ? 20 : 0` from the active ride (or apply the web filter inside DriverLocationService) or correct DECISIONS.md so the record matches the code.

title: Paid pickup wait is added to _paidWaitSeconds only after the Waiting->OnTrip snapshot was persisted, so a crash between the two writes drops the waiting fee
description: `_advanceRide` captures `paidWait = _paidWaitNow`, then awaits `_rideLifecycle.transitionTo(onTrip)`, which immediately writes the snapshot built by `_buildSnapshot` (`paidWaitSeconds: _paidWaitSeconds`, line 39) — still the pre-increment value — and commits stage=onTrip. Only afterwards `_paidWaitSeconds += paidWait` runs and a second `persistNow()` (line 846) writes it. On restore `_paidWaitSeconds = restored?.paidWaitSeconds ?? 0` (accept_ride.dart:609) and the wait clock is no longer running, so `_paidWaitTotal`, `_fareWithWaiting` and the finish journal's `paid` amount lose the pickup waiting fee if the app is killed between the two saves (the second save can also be delayed by a pending background save, active_ride_controller.dart:73-75).
failure_scenario: Driver waited 9 minutes at pickup (4 paid minutes), slides 'Start trip'; the first snapshot (stage onTrip, paidWaitSeconds 0) lands, the process is killed before the second persistNow; after restart the trip resumes on-trip with no paid wait and the completed fare/earnings omit the 4 paid minutes.
suggested_fix: Fold the paid wait into `_paidWaitSeconds` (or into the snapshot builder) before calling `transitionTo`, rolling it back if the transition is refused, so the single stage write already carries the fee.

title: An Exclusive offer held during a Ride check comes back with a fresh full lifetime instead of its remaining time
description: `_onRideCheckGate` (1137-1162) hides an open offer while the Ride check is up and records `_nextTripOfferHeldAt`. After the answer it checks only whether the full lifetime has elapsed since `heldAt` and then calls `_presentOnTripOffer()`, which calls `_armOnTripOfferExpiry()` with `left == null` → `_nextTripOfferDeadline = now + lifetime` (1163-1173). Time already spent before the check (and `_nextTripOfferDeadline`) is ignored, so the rider's offer is held open longer than Dispatch's time to accept; the comment and D-05 say a surviving offer counts down the rest.
failure_scenario: Offer shown with 20 s left; a Ride check opens and is answered after 10 s; the offer returns with the full exclusiveAcceptTime again instead of ~10 s.
evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1157-1161 `if (DateTime.now().difference(heldAt) >= _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); return; }\n      _presentOnTripOffer();` ; 1166-1167 `final time = left ?? _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime;\n      if (left == null) { _nextTripOfferDeadline = _offerNow().add(time); }`
suggested_fix: Keep `_nextTripOfferDeadline` when holding and re-arm with `left: deadline - now` (drop the offer when it is <= 0), as `_resumeOnTripOffer` does.

title: Cancelling the current trip with a secured next trip starts the next AcceptRide without destination mode, unlike completion and the journal snapshot
description: `_submitTripCancellation` builds the next `AcceptRide` (1394-1414) without `destinationModeActive`, `destinationAddress` or `destinationPosition`, whereas `_completeCurrentTrip` (954-956) passes them and the journal's `next` snapshot (`_snapshotForOffer`, 971-979) stores them. After a driver cancel the next trip therefore runs with destination mode off (no on-the-way filter for next-trip offers, the trip options row shows 'next trips on your way' as off), while a crash restore of that same trip from the journal snapshot would restore destination mode on — the two paths disagree.
failure_scenario: Driver has destination mode on, secures a next trip, then ends the current trip early. The next trip's screen has destination mode off; Exclusive offers no longer follow the destination.
evidence:
accept_ride_trip.dart:1394-1414 `AcceptRide(
              tripId: offer.id, ... dispatchRepository: widget.dispatchRepository,
            )` (no destination fields) vs 954-956 `destinationModeActive: _destinationActive,
              destinationAddress: _destinationAddress,
              destinationPosition: _destinationPosition,`
suggested_fix: Pass the three destination fields (or use `AcceptRide.fromPersisted(_snapshotForOffer(offer))` as the rider-cancel path does).

title: Trip island route/guidance face overflows by 22 px at 320 dp wide with 130 % text scale
description: The guidance face of AdaptiveTripIsland (the face the island opens on while a navigation banner is shown; key 'trip-guidance-island') lays out a fixed 74 px route cue plus the guidance text in a Row inside a width clamped to the available 320 dp. With the platform text scale at 1.3 the Row overflows and Flutter raises 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right'. The project's own test test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:470-472 acknowledges this ('The route face it opens on overflows at 320 wide, text 130 %, on main too (a separate finding)') and swallows the exception with a bare tester.takeException(), so the defect is known, untested and shipped. I reproduced it with a throwaway test (since deleted) that pumped the default surface at (320, 1.3), (390, 1.3), (320, 1.0), (360, 1.3): only 320/1.3 raised, output 'AUDIT width=320.0 scale=1.3 exception=A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right.' then 'All tests passed!'. Drivers on a 320 dp phone (e.g. small Android, iPhone SE class) with Large text accessibility setting see a clipped banner with the yellow/black overflow stripes in debug and truncated/overlapping guidance text in release.
failure_scenario: Driver on a 320 dp wide device sets system font size to Large (1.3x). The app opens the trip island on the guidance face during an active trip; the instruction row overflows, guidance text/distance is cut off on the right, and in debug builds the overflow error is thrown every frame.
evidence: lib/presentation/driver/accept ride/adaptive_trip_island.dart:564 `child: Row(` with `SizedBox(width: 74, ...)` cue at ~574; test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:470-472 `// The route face it opens on overflows at 320 wide, text 130 %, on\n// main too (a separate finding); this test is about the default face.\ntester.takeException();`; throwaway run: `AUDIT width=320.0 scale=1.3 exception=A RenderFlex overflowed by 22 pixels on the right.`
suggested_fix: Make the guidance Row's cue column shrinkable (Flexible/FittedBox) or wrap the text in Expanded + FittedBox(scaleDown)/maxLines with ellipsis so the face fits 320 dp at 1.3x; then change the test at line 472 to `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` and add a 320/1.3 guidance-face layout test.

title: Route-progress semantics value is read out in English ('42 percent') in fr/sv
description: The accessibility value of the route progress bar is built as `'${…} percent'` while its label uses `tr.routeProgress`; screen readers in Swedish/French read the English word.
failure_scenario: VoiceOver/TalkBack in Swedish announces 'Ruttframsteg, 42 percent'.
evidence: adaptive_trip_island.dart:1120-1124: `Widget _routeProgress(Color accent, bool available) => Semantics( label: tr.routeProgress, value: available ? '${(widget.progress.clamp(0, 1) * 100).round()} percent' : tr.unavailable,`
suggested_fix: Use `tr.rcPercent(n)` or a dedicated ARB message.

title: Ride check card tells the driver 'Movera safety team alerted · Trip, driver and rider details were sent' while alerts only go to an in-memory demo outbox
description: docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md 'Product truth gate': safety recording/sharing is not a connected service and 'UI must not claim those actions succeeded when only local state changed'. The composition root wires `DemoSafetyAlertRepository` (main.dart:96, an in-memory map/journal) into `RideCheckServices`; `RideCheckController._ensureAlert` marks `_alert` set as soon as that repository returns, and `_alertNote` then renders `tr.moveraSafetyTeamAlerted` + `tr.tripDriverAndRiderDetailsWere` with no demo qualifier, unlike the rating screen ('Rating not sent (demo)') and chat ('Local preview · not sent'). On a red topic (accident, safety concern) the driver is told help was notified when nothing left the phone. Mitigation: a persistent 'demo' banner sits at the top of the app, which is why confidence is low.
failure_scenario: On a trip the Ride check opens (long stop / off route), the driver picks 'Accident or collision' (a red topic): the card shows 'Movera safety team alerted. Trip, driver and rider details were sent.' although only DemoSafetyAlertRepository._alerts was updated.
evidence: ride_check_card.dart:701-714 `text: failed ? tr.moveraCouldNotBeAlerted : tr.moveraSafetyTeamAlerted,` ... `: tr.tripDriverAndRiderDetailsWere,`; main.dart:94-100 `_safetyAlerts = DemoSafetyAlertRepository(); _rideCheck = RideCheckServices(alerts: _safetyAlerts, log: PrefsRideCheckLog());`; demo_safety_alert_repository.dart:155-157 `_alerts[alert.id] = alert; _record('sent', alert, at); return alert;`; app_en.arb:497 `"moveraSafetyTeamAlerted": "Movera safety team alerted"`, :499 `"tripDriverAndRiderDetailsWere": "\nTrip, driver and rider details were sent."`
suggested_fix: Qualify the note while the demo repository is installed (e.g. 'Demo: alert kept on this phone') or expose a `supportsDelivery` flag on SafetyAlertRepository and only claim 'alerted' when a real transport confirms.

title: Re-tapping Continue on Add vehicle after taking document photos silently deletes the saved photos
description: `_save` always upserts the bare identity map `submitted` = {id, make, model, year, plate} (lines 76-85) using the fixed `_vehicleId`. `LocalVehicleStore._upsertSnapshot` replaces the whole row for that id (`rows.removeWhere((row) => row['id'] == vehicle['id']); rows.insert(..., Map.of(vehicle))`, local_vehicle_store.dart) and skips photo fields that are null (`if (value == null) continue;`). After the driver has taken a registration/insurance photo on VehicleDocuments (which upserts the row with `registrationPhoto`/`insurancePhoto`), pressing Back returns to the still-mounted AddVehicle whose `_ready` is still true; tapping Continue again writes the row without the photo keys and the photos are gone. The new VehicleDocuments then restores `_registrationDone = false` and shows 'Recommended next step' again with no message. Reproduced at store level with a throwaway test (upsert identity -> upsert with photo -> upsert identity -> list: `registrationPhoto` absent), test deleted afterwards.
failure_scenario: Vehicles > + > fill make/model/year/plate > Continue > Registration certificate > Take photo (saved locally) > Back > Continue again: the photo row is overwritten; the documents page shows no saved photo and the base64 image is gone from preferences.
evidence: add_vehicle.dart:76-85: `final submitted = <String, dynamic>{ 'id': _vehicleId, 'make': ..., 'model': ..., 'year': _year!, 'plate': ... }; ... await _store.upsert(submitted);`  local_vehicle_store.dart `_upsertSnapshot`: `if (value == null) continue;` ... `rows.removeWhere((row) => row['id'] == vehicle['id']); rows.insert(index < 0 ? rows.length : index, Map.of(vehicle));`
suggested_fix: In `_save`, merge onto the existing row (`{...previousRow, ...submitted}`) or have the store preserve photo fields when the incoming map omits them; alternatively navigate with pushReplacement / disable re-save once the draft exists.

title: Vehicle photo size errors surface the exception's English message in a SnackBar
description: `VehiclePhotoBudgetExceeded` is thrown with English copy in local_vehicle_store.dart:150 ('Photo is too large to keep on this device.') and :170 ('Photo storage on this device is full. Remove photos from another vehicle first.'); add_vehicle.dart catches it and shows `error.message` verbatim, while the generic catch right below uses a localized string.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver attaches a large registration photo: a SnackBar in English appears on an otherwise Swedish screen.
evidence: add_vehicle.dart:498-502: `} on VehiclePhotoBudgetExceeded catch (error) { if (mounted) { ScaffoldMessenger.of(context) .showSnackBar(SnackBar(content: Text(error.message))); }` — local_vehicle_store.dart:149-151: `throw const VehiclePhotoBudgetExceeded( 'Photo is too large to keep on this device.', );`
suggested_fix: Give the exception a code/kind and map it to `tr` in the screen.

title: 'DEMO DATA', 'Central Station → Södermalm', 'Comfort · 21:42' (Analytics), 'DEMO DATA' (Driving log) and 'DRIVING IN' (Documents) are untranslated literals on localized screens
description: These eyebrow labels and sample rows are visible text on screens whose other strings all come from `tr`. analytics.dart:60 'DEMO DATA', :108 'Central Station → Södermalm', :117 'Comfort · 21:42'; driving_logs.dart:50 'DEMO DATA'; documents.dart:76 'DRIVING IN' (the section header above the zone name). No ARB key exists for 'DEMO DATA' or 'DRIVING IN'.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver opens Dokument: a header 'DRIVING IN' sits above 'Stockholm'; Analys and Körlogg both open with an English 'DEMO DATA' badge.
evidence: analytics.dart:59-60: `Text( 'DEMO DATA',` — analytics.dart:107-108: `Text( 'Central Station → Södermalm',` — driving_logs.dart:49-50: `const Text( 'DEMO DATA',` — documents.dart:75-76: `const Text( 'DRIVING IN',`
suggested_fix: Add ARB keys (demoDataBadge, drivingIn, sample trip row) and use them.

title: Onboarding steps are disposed when the driver moves to the next step, so going back loses the picked document/photo and typed vehicle fields
description: The four steps are hosted in `PageView.builder` with default `allowImplicitScrolling = false`, which Flutter 3.47 maps to `ScrollCacheExtent.viewport(0.0)` (page_view.dart:709-710): a page outside the viewport is unmounted. `_VehicleDocumentUploadState` keeps the selection in State (`selectedFileName`, `selectedFileBytes`) and `_AdditionDetailAddVehicleState` keeps its TextEditingControllers in State. After `moveToNextStep` finishes animating, the previous step's State is disposed; `moveToPreviousStep` recreates it from scratch, so the file the driver just picked (and the snackbar said 'File selected successfully') is gone and the year/colour fields are reset to defaults. Reachable only with `MOVERA_ENABLE_LEGACY_AUTH=true` (Sign in > Continue with Apple/Google).
failure_scenario: Legacy auth: Add vehicle step, type year '2019' > Continue > Vehicle registration > Tap to upload, pick a PDF (success snackbar) > Continue > Back: the registration page shows the empty upload area again; Back again: year field is empty.
evidence: navigation.dart:139-146 `PageView.builder( controller: controller.pageController, physics: const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics(), itemCount: controller.pages.length, itemBuilder: (BuildContext context, int index) { return controller.pages[index]; }, )`; vehicle_document_upload.dart:38-39 `String? selectedFileName; Uint8List? selectedFileBytes;` held in State; Flutter page_view.dart:709-710 `scrollCacheExtent ?? ScrollCacheExtent.viewport(allowImplicitScrolling ? 1.0 : 0.0)`.
suggested_fix: Keep step data in the controller (lift `selectedFile*` and the text controllers into `AdditionalInfoNavigationController`) or wrap each page in `AutomaticKeepAliveClientMixin`/set `allowImplicitScrolling: true`.

title: 'Return to home' on the ID preview pops to the first route, which in this flow is the logged-out starter, not Home
description: `DriverStarter` is only reachable from logout (`pushAndRemoveUntil(..., (route) => false)`), so when the legacy flow reaches `TakeIdPhoto` the first route on the stack is the starter (or `DriverSignIn` if the starter was replaced). `Navigator.popUntil((route) => route.isFirst)` therefore lands on the starter/sign-in page while the button is labelled `tr.returnToHome` ('Return to home').
failure_scenario: Legacy auth: Log out > Legacy sign-in > Continue with Google > Verify > Continue > 'Return to home': the app shows the Sign in page (no home).
evidence: take_id_photo.dart:36-38 `Navigator.of(context).popUntil((route) => route.isFirst); }, child: Text(tr.returnToHome),`; profile.dart:414-417 makes DriverStarter the first route.
suggested_fix: Navigate to `DriverRuntimeScope.maybeOf(context)?.homeBuilder()` via pushAndRemoveUntil, or relabel the button.

title: Divider word 'OR' is hardcoded English on the document upload step
description: The upload card uses the literal `"OR"` between 'Tap to upload' and 'Open camera' while the surrounding labels are localized (`tr.tapToUpload`, `tr.openCamera`). French/Swedish users see 'OR'.
failure_scenario: Legacy auth with language Français: 'Appuyez pour téléverser' / 'OR' / 'Ouvrir la caméra'.
evidence: vehicle_document_upload.dart:142-144 `child: TextWidget( text: "OR", color: AppColor.title,`
suggested_fix: Use a localized key for the divider.

title: Document picker loads the whole selected file into memory with no size cap
description: `FilePicker.platform.pickFiles(type: FileType.custom, allowedExtensions: ['pdf','png','jpg','jpeg'], withData: true)` returns the full bytes of whatever file the driver selects and they are kept in `selectedFileBytes` and shown via `Image.memory`. Unlike `_VehiclePhotoPage` (which caps at `LocalVehicleStore.maxPhotoBytes`), there is no size check, so a large scanned PDF or a multi-hundred-MB file is read into Dart heap; on web this can exhaust the tab. Legacy-auth flow only.
failure_scenario: Legacy auth > Vehicle registration > Tap to upload > choose a 300 MB PDF on web: the tab stalls/crashes reading the bytes; on mobile a very large image is decoded by `Image.memory` at full size.
evidence: vehicle_document_upload.dart:238-243 `final result = await FilePicker.platform.pickFiles( type: FileType.custom, allowedExtensions: ['pdf', 'png', 'jpg', 'jpeg'], withData: true, ); file = result?.files.single;` and :251-257 keeps `bytes` with only an `isEmpty` check.
suggested_fix: Check `file.size`/`bytes.length` against a cap (reuse `LocalVehicleStore.maxPhotoBytes` or a document cap) and reject with `_showErrorMessage`.

title: English copy 'Did you don’t get code?' is ungrammatical
description: `tr.didNotGetCode` is rendered on the phone verification screen; the English source string in app_en.arb:2150 is `"Did you don’t get code?"`. French and Swedish translations are correct ('Vous n’avez pas reçu de code ?', 'Fick du ingen kod?'), so only the English UI is broken.
failure_scenario: Legacy auth > Create account > phone > Continue: the screen shows 'Did you don’t get code?'.
evidence: phone_verify.dart:121-122 `TextWidget( text: tr.didNotGetCode,`; lib/l10n/app_en.arb:2150 `"didNotGetCode": "Did you don’t get code?",`
suggested_fix: Change the English string to 'Didn’t get the code?'.

title: Divider word 'or' is hardcoded English and not translated
description: Every other string on the screen goes through `tr`, but the divider uses the literal `"or"`, so French and Swedish users see 'or' between the sign-in options. The app supports en/fr/sv via `AppLocalizations`.
failure_scenario: Set language to Svenska and open Sign in: 'Fortsätt med telefon' / 'or' / 'Fortsätt med Apple'.
evidence: sign_in.dart:61-63 `TextWidget( text: "or", color: AppColor.title,`
suggested_fix: Add an `orWord` key to the arb files and use `tr.orWord`.

title: Legacy sign-in replaces the starter, leaving a screen with no way back to the demo
description: With `MOVERA_ENABLE_LEGACY_AUTH=true`, the starter (the only route after logout, pushed via `pushAndRemoveUntil`) is replaced with `DriverSignIn` through `Navigator.pushReplacement`. `DriverSignIn` has no back button and no 'Return to demo' control, and `BottomToTopTransition` is a bare `ModalRoute` so iOS has no swipe-back. The only exits are deeper preview screens whose Back pops back to DriverSignIn; Android hardware back pops the sole route and closes the app. The 'Return to demo' TextButton that exists on the starter is lost.
failure_scenario: Legacy auth build: Profile > Log out > 'Legacy sign-in preview': the user is stuck on Sign in; on iOS/web there is no way to reach the demo home again without restarting the app.
evidence: starter.dart:79-82 `Navigator.pushReplacement( context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverSignIn()), );`; sign_in.dart has no IconButton/pop and no DriverRuntimeScope use; profile.dart:414-417 `pushAndRemoveUntil(MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => const DriverStarter()), (route) => false)`.
suggested_fix: Use `Navigator.push` (as the registration button already does) or give DriverSignIn a back/return-to-demo action.

title: Destination search result count is the English literal '${results.length} found'
description: While the search field is non-empty the picker shows `'${results.length} found'` next to the localized section title; nothing in the ARB covers it.
failure_scenario: French driver types a destination: header reads 'Résultats   3 found'.
evidence: destination_picker.dart:359-361: `if (_searchController.text.trim().isNotEmpty) Text( '${results.length} found',`
suggested_fix: Add a plural ARB key (e.g. resultsFound) and use it.

title: Section label 'DRIVING IN' is hardcoded English on the Documents screen
description: Documents is a main-path screen (Profile > Documents). Its header eyebrow is `const Text('DRIVING IN', ...)` while the lines under it are localized (`tr.docStockholmTrips`, `tr.docEarnAnywhereSweden`), so French/Swedish drivers see an English label above a translated title.
failure_scenario: Language Svenska > Profile > Documents: 'DRIVING IN' above 'Stockholm-resor'.
evidence: documents.dart:75-76 `const Text( 'DRIVING IN',`
suggested_fix: Add an arb key and use `tr`.

title: feeSuffix hardcodes 'kr' for whole-unit cancel fees regardless of the fee's currency
description: `feeSuffix(Money? fee)` prints `'${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'` whenever the amount is a whole number of minor-hundreds, ignoring `fee.currency` and its exponent (Money supports SEK/EUR with exponent 2 and TND with exponent 3; zone_settings maps EUR->FR and TND->TN). Only the non-whole branch uses `fee.formatted`. Callers: reservationCancelled island message (line 60-66), RiderCancelledSheet status line (rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:59-62), ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:678). The fee is the backend's decision (R15-7) in the zone currency.
failure_scenario: In a French zone the backend sends cancelFee {amountMinor: 500, currency: 'EUR'}: the island and the rider-cancelled sheet say '· +5 kr' instead of '· +5,00 €'; for TND 5000 millimes they say '+50 kr' instead of '5,000 DT'.
evidence: lib/presentation/driver/home/components/home_island_notices.dart:72-74 `final amount = fee.minorUnits % 100 == 0\n        ? '${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'\n        : fee.formatted;`
suggested_fix: Use `fee.formattedShort` (already drops a zero fraction and keeps the currency symbol/exponent) for both branches.

title: IslandMessages.posted grows without bound in production: every show() appends and only the test-only reset() clears it
description: `posted` is @visibleForTesting but show() unconditionally does `posted.add(message)` (line 76) in the production path; nothing in the app ever calls reset(). Each IslandMessage holds a title string and often a closure (onTap) that captures the Home state. Over a long online session (online/offline, matching, waiting tips are not posted here, but every match/taken/unavailable/cash/reminder/notification message is) the list keeps growing and keeps old State closures alive.
failure_scenario: A driver keeps the app open for a long shift: every island message ever posted (and the closures of disposed Home states after logout/login) stays referenced in a static list until the process dies.
evidence: island_messages.dart:72-76 `@visibleForTesting static final List<IslandMessage> posted = <IslandMessage>[]; static void show(IslandMessage message) { posted.add(message);` | island_messages.dart:94-98 `@visibleForTesting static void reset() { _queue.clear(); posted.clear(); }`
suggested_fix: Only record into `posted` under a test flag (kDebugMode/visibleForTesting hook) or cap its length.

title: Reservation sheet hardcodes the English plural "N stops" instead of the localized tr.stopsCount
description: The stops line uses `tr.n1Stop` for one stop but the string literal `'${request.stops.length} stops'` for more, while the app ships sv and fr ARBs with `stopsCount` plural forms (app_sv.arb:714 "{count} stopp", app_fr.arb:714 "{count} arrêts") and RadarOfferView.stopsLabel already uses `tr.stopsCount(stops)` (radar_offer_card.dart:105-106). A Swedish or French driver sees "2 stops" on the Home reservation request.
failure_scenario: App language Swedish, reservation request with two stops rises on Home: the sheet reads "2 stops" under the pickup instead of "2 stopp".
evidence: reservation_request_sheet.dart:277-281 `stops: _show.stops && request.stops.isNotEmpty ? (request.stops.length == 1 ? tr.n1Stop : '${request.stops.length} stops') : null,` | radar_offer_card.dart:105-106 `String get stopsLabel => stops <= 0 ? '' : tr.stopsCount(stops);`
suggested_fix: Use `tr.stopsCount(request.stops.length)`.

title: AppLifecycleState.inactive is treated as not foreground, so Home renders the driver as offline (radar "OFF · Tap to scan", offline dock, no "Finding trips") while the session is online
description: didChangeAppLifecycleState sets `_foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed` (line 189); _isOnline (line 335) is `_liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && availableForOffers`, and the radar layer, dock, side menu and island all branch on _isOnline (home_map_sheet.dart:1654-1694, 1594, home.dart:713). `inactive` is a visible state: iOS during a phone call banner, Control Center/notification centre, Face ID prompt, app switcher; Android during a system dialog, the location-permission dialog, multi-window without focus. In all of these the app is on screen and after _pauseHomeUpdates() (line 190) it draws the offline face, cancels the dispatch subscription and offer timers, although DriverSessionController still says online and dispatch still sends offers. On return it snaps back. An incoming phone call while online is a routine driver situation.
failure_scenario: Driver is online on Home; a phone call comes in on iOS (app stays visible behind the call banner, state = inactive). Home immediately shows "Radar · OFF · Tap to scan" and the offline dock for the whole call; the driver believes they were taken offline. When the call ends, the online face returns. Offers arriving during the call were not listed.
evidence: home.dart:187-191 `void didChangeAppLifecycleState(AppLifecycleState state) { _foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed; if (_liveVisible) { _resumeHomeUpdates(); } else { _pauseHomeUpdates(); } }` | home.dart:335 `bool get _isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers;` | home_map_sheet.dart:1686-1694 `child: _isOnline ? (holdOff ? _holdOffRadar() : ...) : _isGoingOnline ? _buildGoingOnlineButton() : _buildGoOnlineButton(),`
suggested_fix: Treat `inactive` as foreground for rendering (only `paused`/`hidden`/`detached` pause updates), or keep rendering from the session state and use _liveVisible only to gate timers/subscriptions.

title: _activateDestinationMode continues after its awaits without re-checking mounted/destination state and goes online anyway
description: After the synchronous setup, `_activateDestinationMode` awaits `_refreshDestinationRoadRoute()` (a network road-route request) and `_fitDestinationRoute()` (341-342) and then unconditionally runs `_seedDemoDestinationTrips()`, `_maybeShowSoonReservation()` and `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }` (343-348). The inner helpers guard themselves, but `_goOnline` (home.dart 884-930) has no `mounted` check and calls `showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)`, `setState(...)`, `_startDriverLocation` and arms timers. If the driver turned the destination off during the fetch (island → details sheet → "Turn off destination" → `_endDestinationMode`, or the admin time limit timer at 313-318 fired) the driver is still switched online because of a destination that no longer exists; if Home was disposed during the await, `setState`/`context` are used after dispose.
failure_scenario: Driver confirms a destination, the road-route request is slow, and within those seconds they open the island sheet and tap "Turn off destination". The route request returns, and `_goOnline()` flips the driver online (radar starts, offers arrive) although destination mode is off and they never asked to go online.
evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart 341-348: `await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute(); await _fitDestinationRoute(); _seedDemoDestinationTrips(); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._maybeShowSoonReservation(); if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }`
home.dart 884-887: `void _goOnline() { if (_driverSession.isSuspended) { IslandMessages.show(...); unawaited(showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)); return; }` (no mounted guard)
suggested_fix: After the awaits add `if (!mounted || !_destinationModeActive || _destinationPosition != destination) { return; }` before seeding/going online (the same guard `_fitDestinationRoute` already uses at 404-406).

title: `home_island_hint_seen` is written through SharedPreferences but is missing from localDataInventory and survives logout
description: local_data.dart:38 declares `localDataInventory` as the 'Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences' and clearLocalUserData removes only inventoried keys. `_showIslandHintOnce` writes `prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true)` directly, outside the inventory and outside the SettingsRepository sections, so it is neither documented nor cleared. LOCAL_DATA.md says logout removes 'settings'; this per-driver first-launch setting is kept, and the next driver signing in on the same device never gets the one-time earnings hint the islandHint feature exists to show. The inventory test (test/core/local_data_test.dart) only checks that listed keys are listed, so it cannot catch unlisted writers.
failure_scenario: Driver A sees the island hint once; A logs out (LOCAL_DATA.md: settings cleared); driver B on the same phone/browser never sees the first-launch hint because `flutter.home_island_hint_seen` is still true.
evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:26 `const String _islandHintSeenKey = 'home_island_hint_seen';`; home_map_sheet.dart:1337-1339 `final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance(); if (!mounted || (prefs.getBool(_islandHintSeenKey) ?? false)) { return; } await prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true);`; local_data.dart:38-41 `/// Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences.` with no such record; local_data.dart:123-132 `const exact = <String>[ PrefsActiveRideRepository.key, ... DriverStartPosition.key ];`
suggested_fix: Add the key to localDataInventory (class preference) and to the logout clear list, or store it as a SettingsRepository section so the existing prefix clear covers it.

title: Expired Radar offers dropped by _refreshRadarHomeOffers keep their entry in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers, so the same offer re-listed later never gets a pick window
description: _refreshRadarHomeOffers removes offers in _radarOfferExpired from the list and clears _radarOfferExpired and their _radarOfferDeadlines (400-404), but leaves the fired Timer objects in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers (only _dismissRadarHomeOffer and _cancelAllOfferTimers remove them). _startRadarPickWindow returns early whenever `_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id)` (425-428). An offer with the same id that comes back onto the deck (the demo's _showDispatchOfferAt(0..2) re-run on every _resumeHomeUpdates for nearby-1..3 which stay in the feed; a reservation re-joining via _reservationToDeck) is listed with no deadline and no timer, so its Match never fades.
failure_scenario: nearby-1's 15 s window runs out, a pending trip triggers a refresh (nearby-1 leaves). Driver opens and closes a side-menu screen; _scheduleVisibleOffers re-lists nearby-1. Its card now shows an active Match indefinitely instead of expiring after the radar time.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:400-404 `next.removeWhere((offer) => _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)); _radarOfferExpired.clear(); _radarOfferDeadlines.removeWhere((id, _) => !next.any((offer) => offer.id == id));` | home_offer_radar.dart:424-428 `void _startRadarPickWindow(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id) || _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)) { return; }`
suggested_fix: Remove (and cancel) the _radarOfferTimeoutTimers entry for every offer dropped in _refreshRadarHomeOffers, or key the early-return on an active (not yet fired) timer.

title: A Match claim that succeeds after the driver went offline is silently discarded although dispatch assigned the trip
description: While a Radar claim is in flight the radar orb is still wrapped in _radarLongPressOff (home_map_sheet.dart:1689, 1716-1723) and the island long press also offers "Go offline?" (1110-1116). _goOffline() calls _HomeOfferRadar._cancelAllOfferTimers() without preserveClaim (home.dart:949), which sets _homeRadarMatchingOfferId = null (home_offer_radar.dart:796-800). When _dispatch.claimOffer later resolves with ClaimOutcome.success, _claimHomeRadarOffer returns at line 546 because `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id`; nothing tells dispatch and nothing is shown. In the demo repository the offer was already removed from the feed by the claim (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566), i.e. it is taken by this driver. The driver is offline, the rider is matched to a driver who is not coming.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Match, then long-presses the radar and confirms "Go offline" before dispatch answers (slow network). Dispatch answers success → the trip is assigned to this driver server-side; the app shows nothing, stays offline, never opens the trip and never declines/cancels it.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:542-546 `result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(offer.id); ... if (!mounted || _homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id) { return; }` | home.dart:949 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._cancelAllOfferTimers();` | home_offer_radar.dart:796-800 `if (!preserveClaim) { _homeRadarMatchingOfferId = null; _claimedHomeOffer = null; _homeRadarMatchStates.clear(); }` | home_map_sheet.dart:1689-1691 `_radarLongPressOff(front != null ? _acceptRadar(front) : _buildTripRadarButton())`
suggested_fix: Either block going offline while a claim is in flight (disable the long press / show "please wait"), or keep the claim across _goOffline and, on a late success, open the trip or send dispatch a decline/cancel for that offer.

title: Two Radar offers lost in the same dispatch update share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer, so only the last one is removed and the others stay as "Taken" cards indefinitely
description: _watchDispatchRadar's listener loops over every listed/pending offer missing from the new snapshot and calls _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost for each (604-611). _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost marks the offer claimedElsewhere and arms the single field _homeRadarLostMatchTimer after `_homeRadarLostMatchTimer?.cancel()` (691-702). The second call cancels the first offer's dismissal, so that offer keeps state claimedElsewhere, stays in _radarHomeOffers (shown blurred/"Taken"), keeps _hasRideOffers true (radar "trips found", island green ring) and is only removed by a manual ×, a pause/resume (_resumeOfferTimers) or going offline. _refreshRadarHomeOffers never drops claimedElsewhere offers. Concrete demo path: two destination-mode trips on the deck (home_map_sheet.dart:463-465), then "Turn off destination" → _clearDemoDestinationTrips → DemoDispatchRepository.clearDestinationTrips emits a snapshot without both (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:614-624) → both resolved lost in one loop. With a real feed any update that drops two listed offers at once does the same.
failure_scenario: Driver has two deck cards from destination mode and turns destination mode off. Both cards are marked taken; after 2.8 s only the second disappears, the first stays as a greyed "Taken by another driver" card and the radar keeps saying trips are found until the driver taps × or goes offline.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:604-611 `for (final offer in [..._radarHomeOffers, ..._pendingRadarHomeOffers]) { if (!ids.contains(offer.id) && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == _HomeRadarMatchState.available) { _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost(offer, _RadarOfferGone.unavailable); } }` | home_offer_radar.dart:691-702 `_homeRadarLostMatchTimer?.cancel(); _homeRadarLostMatchTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 2800), () { ... _dismissRadarHomeOffer(offer); });`
suggested_fix: Keep one dismissal timer per offer id (a Map<String, Timer> like _radarOfferTimeoutTimers), or have the timer dismiss every offer currently in claimedElsewhere state.

title: Closing (×) the Radar card whose Match claim is in flight leaves Home permanently in "Matching": no other trip can be matched and the won claim is dropped
description: RadarOfferCard always shows the corner × on Home (onClose is always passed; radar_offer_card.dart:589-616 draws it regardless of `state`, including `matching`). _closeRadarHomeOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:890-896) calls _dismissRadarHomeOffer, which removes the offer from _radarHomeOffers and _homeRadarMatchStates (479-492) but never clears _homeRadarMatchingOfferId or _claimedHomeOffer. From then on: every other card's onMatch is null (`blocked != null && blocked != id ? null : ...`, 1127-1129), the radar orb is `busy` ("Matching · please wait", home_map_sheet.dart:1753-1774), _canStartScheduled is false so a scheduled "Leave now" goes to the backup driver (home_scheduled.dart:166-170, 177-178). When the dispatch claim resolves successfully, _claimHomeRadarOffer passes its guard (`_homeRadarMatchingOfferId == offer.id`), _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer and _openClaimedHomeOffer → 850 ms → _acceptRadarHomeOffer returns because the offer is no longer in _radarHomeOffers (925-928). _claimedHomeOffer stays set, so every later _scheduleVisibleOffers (resume) returns early at 1167-1170. The only exit is going offline (which runs _cancelAllOfferTimers without preserveClaim). The same path is reachable through _setAcceptsCash/_onCategoriesChanged, which dismiss listed offers regardless of claim state (home_offer_rules.dart:31-35, 52-56). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (two offers on the deck, Match on `first`, tap `radar-offer-close`, then complete the claim with ClaimResult.success): AcceptRide never opened, `radar-match-second` onPressed stayed null and the orb read "Matching" 30 s later. Test result: `00:07 +2: All tests passed!`.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Match on a Radar card, then (within the claim's network latency) taps the small × on that card. Dispatch answers success: the trip is assigned to this driver on the server, but no trip opens; the remaining cards' Match buttons are disabled and the radar says "Matching / please wait" indefinitely. The driver cannot accept any trip until they go offline and online again; a scheduled "Leave now" in that state is handed to a backup driver.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:890-896 `void _closeRadarHomeOffer(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (offer.groupId != null && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == _HomeRadarMatchState.available) { unawaited(_dispatch.declineOffer(offer.id)); } _dismissRadarHomeOffer(offer); }` | home_offer_radar.dart:483-492 `_rebuild(() { _radarHomeOffers.removeWhere((item) => item.id == offer.id); ... _homeRadarMatchStates.remove(offer.id); ...` (no _homeRadarMatchingOfferId / _claimedHomeOffer reset) | home_offer_radar.dart:925-928 `void _acceptRadarHomeOffer(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (!_radarHomeOffers.any((item) => item.id == offer.id)) { return; } ...` | home_offer_radar.dart:1127-1129 `onMatch: blocked != null && blocked != id ? null : () => _startHomeRadarMatch(offer),` | home_offer_radar.dart:1167-1171 `if (_claimedHomeOffer != null) { _openClaimedHomeOffer(); return; } if (_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != null) { return; }` | radar_offer_card.dart:589-591 `final close = onClose; if (close == null) { return card; } return Stack(`
suggested_fix: Refuse × (and rule-driven dismissals) while `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId == offer.id` (pass onClose: null for a matching card), or make _dismissRadarHomeOffer clear _homeRadarMatchingOfferId/_claimedHomeOffer and cancel _homeRadarNoticeTimer when it removes the matching offer; and let _acceptRadarHomeOffer open the trip from _claimedHomeOffer even if the card was removed.

title: Re-showing the Exclusive offer already on screen restarts its countdown; the demo _directOfferTimer re-fires on every resume, so returning from any route resets the offer's time to the full lifetime (contradicts the D-04/R13-3 "time left" rule)
description: _showOutsideRadarOffer lets an offer whose id equals the current _outsideRadarOffer through its guard (232) and then cancels _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer and calls _raiseExclusive → _startExclusiveClock, which resets the clock to 1 and the deadline to now+lifetime (251-259, home_exclusive.dart:89-93). _resumeHomeUpdates (home.dart:204-213) first restores the time left via _resumeOfferTimers → _resumeExclusiveTimeout, but it also calls _scheduleVisibleOffers, which re-arms _directOfferTimer (2.2 s) to show the demo Exclusive again (1175-1189). If the same offer is still up (e.g. the driver dismissed the Go-offline dialog, or came back from Ride history inside the 15 s), 2.2 s later its ring and pill jump back to 15 s. _seedDemoDestinationTrips (home_map_sheet.dart:458-466) and _releasePendingRadarOffers → _pendingAdminAssign have the same re-show shape.
failure_scenario: Exclusive offer shows 9 s left; driver long-presses the radar, gets "Go offline?", taps "Stay online". The offer resumes at ~8 s, then 2.2 s later jumps back to 15 s and the Q16 miss clock runs again from scratch.
evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:232 `(_outsideRadarOffer != null && _outsideRadarOffer!.id != offer.id) ||` | home_offer_radar.dart:251-259 `_outsideOfferTimeoutTimer?.cancel(); final arriving = _outsideRadarOffer?.id != offer.id; _rebuild(() { _outsideRadarOffer = offer; }); ... _HomeExclusive(this)._raiseExclusive(offer, lifetime);` | home_exclusive.dart:89-93 `_exclusive.clock.duration = lifetime; _exclusive.deadline = ScheduledClock.realNow().add(lifetime); unawaited(_exclusive.clock.reverse(from: 1));` | home.dart:208-209 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._scheduleVisibleOffers(); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._resumeOfferTimers();`
suggested_fix: In _showOutsideRadarOffer return early when `_outsideRadarOffer?.id == offer.id` (the offer is already up), so only a new offer starts a clock.

title: A won Exclusive reservation / admin-assign claim is marked taken and then dropped when Home is covered by another route at the moment the claim resolves
description: _claimExclusiveReservation (home_reservation.dart:484-509) and _claimAdminAssign (home_offer_radar.dart:843-860) await dispatch, then on success call ScheduledRideStore.take(offer.id) / show "matched" and _openOfferTrip, which pushes via pushSingle (home_offer_radar.dart:940). pushSingle silently does nothing when Home is not the current route (single_route_entry.dart:11-13). During the claim the Exclusive sheet covers the dock, but the Scaffold drawer is still reachable by edge swipe (it is not a route) and its items push screens (Ride history, Wallet, …). The claim result then arrives while a route covers Home: the reservation has left Scheduled rides (take()), _reservation.wonId is set, _outsideRadarOffer is cleared in the post-frame callback, and no trip opens. Unlike the Radar deck path (_openClaimedHomeOffer waits for _liveVisible and is retried from _scheduleVisibleOffers), these two paths have no deferral/retry.
failure_scenario: Exclusive reservation (or admin direct assign) is up, driver taps Accept, edge-swipes the drawer and opens Ride history while the claim is pending. Dispatch answers success: the reservation disappears from Scheduled rides and from Home, the island says "accepted", but no trip screen ever opens and nothing is persisted; on the server the trip is this driver's.
evidence: home_reservation.dart:505-509 `ScheduledRideStore.take(offer.id); _reservation.wonId = offer.id; IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.reservationAccepted); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._acceptOutsideRadarOffer();` | home_offer_radar.dart:858-860 `case ClaimOutcome.success: IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.matched); _openOfferTrip(offer, ExclusiveReasons.text(ExclusiveReasons.assigned));` | home_offer_radar.dart:940 `pushSingle(` | single_route_entry.dart:11-13 `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }`
suggested_fix: Route won Exclusive claims through the same deferred handoff as the Radar deck (_claimedHomeOffer + _openClaimedHomeOffer, retried from _scheduleVisibleOffers/didPopNext), and have _openOfferTrip verify that pushSingle actually pushed before clearing state.

title: "Leave now" removes the accepted scheduled ride from the store before a push that silently does nothing when Home is not the current route
description: `_planScheduled` arms `Timer(_clock.realUntil(start), () => _leaveNow(ride))` (line 161). These timers live in `_scheduled.timers`, which `_pauseHomeUpdates` (home.dart 192-203) never cancels, and `_leaveNow`/`_canStartScheduled` (lines 166-170, 175-189) only check `mounted`, `_recoveryResolved`, `_driverSession.availableForOffers`, `_claimedHomeOffer` and `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId`; neither `_routeVisible` nor `ModalRoute.isCurrent` is consulted. `availableForOffers` is `_status == online` (driver_session_controller.dart 34), which stays true while the driver is on any non-trip screen pushed over Home (Scheduled rides, Notifications, Settings, Support, Wallet, Ride history, a modal sheet such as the destination details sheet or the queue sheet). When the timer fires in that state, `_startScheduledTrip` (218-239) first calls `ScheduledRideStore.start(ride)` which is `_removeAccepted(ride) != null` (scheduled_rides.dart 638-660) and permanently drops the ride from Accepted, posts the "Leave now" island message and notification, and only then calls `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(...)` (home_offer_radar.dart 931-981) whose `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...)))` returns `Future.value()` without pushing because `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` (single_route_entry.dart 11-13). `_planScheduled()` then re-plans for the *next* ride. Nothing re-opens or restores the removed ride; `didPopNext` only re-runs `_restoreActiveRideIfNeeded`, and no AcceptRide/persisted trip was ever created.
failure_scenario: Driver is online, has an accepted reservation for 07:40, and at 07:0x opens Scheduled rides (or any other screen/sheet) over Home to check it. The "leave now" moment arrives while that screen is on top: the ride disappears from Scheduled rides › Accepted, the island later flashes "Leave now for 07:40" and a notification "Leave now for 07:40 pickup" appears, but no trip screen ever opens; returning to Home shows no trip and the ride is gone for good (no backup hand-off either, since `_scheduled.ride` was set to null).
evidence:
home_scheduled.dart 166-170: `bool get _canStartScheduled => _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers && _claimedHomeOffer == null && _homeRadarMatchingOfferId == null;`
home_scheduled.dart 218-237: `final started = ScheduledRideStore.start(ride); ... if (!started) { return; } _scheduled..ride = null..lateSince = null; ... _HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide); _planScheduled();`
scheduled_rides.dart 638-639: `static bool start(ReservationRequestPreview ride) => _removeAccepted(ride) != null;`
home_offer_radar.dart 940-942: `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(`
single_route_entry.dart 11-13: `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }`
home.dart 192-203 (`_pauseHomeUpdates`) cancels offer/radar timers only; `_scheduled.timers` keep running while Home is covered.
suggested_fix: Make `_canStartScheduled` require Home to be current/visible (e.g. `_routeVisible && ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == true`) and treat the not-current case like `_lateScheduled`/defer; or defer `_leaveNow` until `didPopNext` (store a pending ride and run it in `_resumeHomeUpdates`). Alternatively only call `ScheduledRideStore.start(ride)` after `pushSingle` has actually pushed (check its return/`navigator` state) and roll back on a no-op push.

title: "Leave now" removes the accepted scheduled ride from Accepted and then drops the trip when Home is not the current route (pushSingle no-ops)
description: _leaveNow() fires from a Timer planned in _planScheduled(). Its only guard is _canStartScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:166-170: _recoveryResolved, availableForOffers, no claim in flight); it never checks that Home is the current route. _startScheduledTrip() first calls ScheduledRideStore.start(ride) (line 220), which removes the ride from Accepted (scheduled_rides.dart:638-639 / 652-660), posts "Leave now" and then calls _HomeOfferRadar._openOfferTrip (line 234). _openOfferTrip cancels every offer timer and calls pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...))) (home_offer_radar.dart:940). pushSingle returns Future.value() without pushing when `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` or while another push's entry animation is running (single_route_entry.dart:11-15). The return value is ignored, the post-frame callback clears the offers, _planScheduled() moves on to the next ride. Nothing is persisted (AcceptRide is what writes the active-ride snapshot), so the ride is gone from the phone: not in Accepted, not an active trip. Home's didPopNext restore only re-opens persisted snapshots, so returning to Home does not recover it. Any pushed route over Home triggers this: Scheduled rides screen (where a driver is likely to be looking at exactly this ride), Wallet, Preferences, Support inbox, Ride history, Notifications, Documents, the Go-offline confirm dialog, the driving-time/performance/waybill/destination/safety modal sheets. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (fast demo day, ride accepted, a MaterialPageRoute pushed over Home at ~07:33, then 12 s): `Leave now for 07:40 pickup` was posted, ScheduledRideStore.upcoming no longer contained the ride, find.byType(AcceptRide) was findsNothing before and after popping the covering route. Test result: `00:07 +2: All tests passed!`.
failure_scenario: Driver has accepted the 07:40 reservation, is online, and opens Scheduled rides (or any other screen) at 07:33. The smart-gap timer fires "Leave now": the ride leaves Accepted, the island (hidden) says "Leave now", no trip screen opens. Driver returns to Home: no active trip, the reservation is no longer in Accepted, nothing is persisted. The rider's ride is silently lost on this phone.
evidence: home_scheduled.dart:166-170 `bool get _canStartScheduled => _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers && _claimedHomeOffer == null && _homeRadarMatchingOfferId == null;` | home_scheduled.dart:218-222 `_scheduled.planning = true; final started = ScheduledRideStore.start(ride); ... if (!started) { return; }` | home_scheduled.dart:234-237 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide);` | home_offer_radar.dart:940-943 `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(` | single_route_entry.dart:11-13 `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }` | scheduled_rides.dart:638-639 `static bool start(ReservationRequestPreview ride) => _removeAccepted(ride) != null;`
suggested_fix: In _leaveNow/_startScheduledTrip require Home to be visible and current (e.g. `_liveVisible && ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == true`), otherwise treat it like a pause: keep the ride in Accepted and retry from didPopNext/_resumeHomeUpdates (_onRadarLive already re-plans). Alternatively make _openOfferTrip check pushSingle's outcome and roll back (re-add the ride / not clear offers) when nothing was pushed.

title: Queue position sheet shows hard-coded English '15-30 mins EST time'
description: The sheet opened from `in_airport_queue.dart:20` (`showMyQueuePositionSheet`) localizes its title (`tr.queueMediumWait`) but the line under it is a literal English string with a non-standard abbreviation.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver opens Min plats i kön: 'Medellång väntan' followed by '15-30 mins EST time'.
evidence: my_queue_pos.dart:113-121: `TextWidget( text: tr.queueMediumWait, ...), 2.height, TextWidget( text: "15-30 mins EST time",`
suggested_fix: Add an ARB key and use `tr`.

title: Native: the map padding switches between the 75% driving anchor and the plain top inset the instant a pan is reported or recenter starts, which the SDK realizes as an immediate content shift under the finger and a snap at the start of the 'no snap' recenter flight
description: On native the 75% vehicle anchor is realized through `GoogleMap.padding` (`drivingInsets(... following:)` returns a top inset of `2*desired - height + bottom`, roughly 520 px on an 800 px screen with a 260 px top and 120 px sheet, versus 260 px when not following). `accept_ride.dart:1227-1234` passes `following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following`. `onUserGesture` (`accept_ride.dart:1242`) runs `_rebuild(_camera.userGesture)`, so on the first 6 px of a drag the widget rebuilds with the smaller top padding; Android `setPadding` and iOS `GMSMapView.padding` keep the camera target lat/lng and re-centre it in the new padded region, i.e. the map content jumps by about (520-260)/2 = 130 px while the driver's finger is on it. On recenter the padding flips back before the eased 1 s flight (`google_driver_camera_port.dart:102-106` documents the flight as landing with no snap), so the flight starts with an instant jump. The web path is guarded (`drivingInsets` returns `edgeInsets` on web and the JS `configure` only pans when `state.anchored`, which `release()` has already cleared); the native path has no equivalent guard. Not executable here (needs a device), hence the modest confidence.
failure_scenario: Driver in guidance on Android/iOS starts dragging the map: as soon as the drag registers (6 px) the whole map lurches ~130 px up under the finger; tapping recenter produces an equal downward jump before the smooth flight begins.
evidence: map_overlay_insets.dart:25-47: `EdgeInsets drivingInsets(double height, {required bool following}) { if (kIsWeb) { return edgeInsets; } ... final desired = (height * .75).clamp(top + margin, height - bottom - margin); return EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(32, following ? math.max(top, 2 * desired - height + bottom) : top, 32, bottom);`. accept_ride.dart:1227-1234: `padding: MapOverlayInsets.forActiveRide(...).drivingInsets(MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).height, following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following), cameraAnchor: ... ? .75 : .5,`. accept_ride.dart:1242: `onUserGesture: () { _rebuild(_camera.userGesture); ...`.
suggested_fix: Keep the native padding constant across follow/browse (the anchor is only needed for follow frames, which the port can realize by offsetting the camera target instead), or defer the padding change until the gesture ends and apply it together with the first camera move.

title: Saved ride-category choice is never applied after an app restart until the driver reopens Ride preferences
description: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` (the set offers are filtered by: home_offer_rules.dart `_offerAllowed`/`_rideAllowed` -> `DriverCategoryChoice.takes`) is only populated by `_publishChoice()` which runs from `_restoreSettings` (line 122) and `_toggle` (line 183) inside the Preferences screen. Nothing reads the `'categories'` settings section at startup: `main.dart` restores only `MapTrafficSetting.restore()` (line 41) and `DriverLanguage.restore()` (line 46); grep shows `read('categories')` exists only in preferences.dart. So the screen says '{n} ride categories saved' and persists the choice, but after a cold start `off` is `const {}` and the driver receives offers of every category they switched off, until they happen to open Ride preferences again.
failure_scenario: Driver switches off 'Priority' and 'Comfort' in Ride preferences (snackbar '4 ride categories saved'), kills and relaunches the app, goes online: Priority/Comfort offers appear on Home and in the Live list; reopening Ride preferences shows them correctly off and only then stops the offers.
evidence: preferences.dart:171-176 `void _publishChoice() { DriverCategoryChoice.off.value = { for (final index in _visible) if (!_selected[index]) _categories[index].title, }; }` is the only writer; ride_categories.dart `static final ValueNotifier<Set<String>> off = ValueNotifier<Set<String>>(const <String>{});`; main.dart:41 `unawaited(MapTrafficSetting.restore());` / :46 `await DriverLanguage.restore()...` with no categories restore.
suggested_fix: Move the restore/publish logic into a `DriverCategoryChoice.restore(SettingsRepository)` and call it from the app root at startup next to MapTrafficSetting/DriverLanguage; Preferences keeps using the same code.

title: Toggling the last category off is persisted and published immediately although the Save button refuses a zero selection
description: `_toggle` has no minimum-selection guard: it flips `_selected[index]`, calls `_publishChoice()` and `_persistSettings()` on every tap. Only the explicit Save button is disabled when `_selectedCount == 0` (line 465) and its border goes grey, suggesting that state is not accepted. But the auto-save has already written `selected: [false, ...]` to storage and set `DriverCategoryChoice.off` to every visible category, so `_rideAllowed`/`_offerAllowed` reject every offer: the driver can go online and never receive a ride, with the screen implying the zero state was never saved.
failure_scenario: Open Ride preferences, tap every card off (header '0 of 6 active', Save greyed), press Back, go online: no offers arrive at all; relaunching Preferences restores the all-off state from storage.
evidence: preferences.dart:178-185 `void _toggle(int index) { if (!_canEdit) return; setState(() { _selected[index] = !_selected[index]; }); _publishChoice(); _persistSettings(); }`; :465-467 `onPressed: !_canEdit || _explicitSaving || _selectedCount == 0 ? null : _save,`
suggested_fix: Either refuse the toggle that would leave zero visible categories (keep at least one on, as the Save guard implies) or make the Save state honest (allow saving zero, or show that nothing is saved).

title: '1 ride categories saved' – the saved-count snackbar is not pluralized
description: `tr.prefCategoriesSaved(selectedCount)` is a plain placeholder string `"{count} ride categories saved"` (app_en.arb:2601; sv/fr likewise) rather than an ICU plural like `inDaysCount`. With exactly one category enabled, Save announces '1 ride categories saved' ('1 resekategorier sparade').
failure_scenario: Leave only 'Movera' on and tap Save preferences: snackbar '1 ride categories saved'.
evidence: preferences.dart:203 `tr.prefCategoriesSaved(selectedCount),`; app_en.arb:2601 `"prefCategoriesSaved": "{count} ride categories saved"`
suggested_fix: Convert to `{count, plural, =1{1 ride category saved} other{{count} ride categories saved}}` in all arbs.

title: Profile shows 'Vehicle data unavailable' while the vehicle identity is still loading
description: The Vehicles link detail is `snapshot.data?.vehicle ?? tr.vehicleDataUnavailable` with no check of `snapshot.connectionState`. `primaryIdentity()` is async (SharedPreferences read through the serialized settings queue), so every open of Profile first paints the error text 'Vehicle data unavailable' and then replaces it with the vehicle name; after `_vehicleChanged` the same flash repeats. The same text is meant for the read-failure case (`primaryIdentity` returns null on error).
failure_scenario: Open Profile: the Vehicles row reads 'Vehicle data unavailable' for a frame or more, then 'Mercedes-Benz E 220'.
evidence: profile.dart:156-166 `FutureBuilder<...>( future: _identity, builder: (context, snapshot) => _link( ... detail: snapshot.data?.vehicle ?? tr.vehicleDataUnavailable, ...`
suggested_fix: Show an empty/loading detail while `snapshot.connectionState != ConnectionState.done`.

title: Logout clears the saved category preferences but leaves the in-memory offer filter, so the next session filters offers by the previous driver's choice
description: Logout runs `runtime.logout` (main.dart:180-193) which calls `clearLocalUserData()` (removes every `movera_driver_settings_section_*` key incl. 'categories') and resets `MapTrafficSetting` and `DriverLanguage`, but never calls `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`. `DriverCategoryChoice.off` therefore keeps the switched-off set after logout and 'Return to demo'. Home's `_startAccount` only listens to the notifier, so offers of those categories stay hidden while a reopened Preferences screen shows all categories on (storage was cleared) and only then republishes an empty set. LOCAL_DATA.md says logout removes settings; this derived state survives.
failure_scenario: Switch off 'Comfort' in Ride preferences, Profile > Log out > Return to demo, go online: Comfort offers are still filtered out although Ride preferences (storage) now shows every category enabled; opening Ride preferences once makes them reappear.
evidence: profile.dart:393-394 `if (runtime?.logout != null) { await runtime!.logout!(); }`; main.dart:185-186 `MapTrafficSetting.reset(); DriverLanguage.reset();` (no `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`); ride_categories.dart `static void reset() => off.value = const <String>{};` exists but is unused by logout (grep: no callers in lib/).
suggested_fix: Call `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()` (and reset the other derived demo singletons such as DocumentExpiryStore/DriverNotificationFeed if intended) in `_MoveraAppState._logout`.

title: Cancelled trip detail shows the quoted fare as 'Ride cost' and a Movera bonus note the driver never earned
description: `_buildSummaryRows` always renders `_detailRow(tr.rideCost, _ride.fare)` and, when `driverBonus` is set, the 'incl. +X kr Movera bonus' note (line 400-416), regardless of `_ride.status`. History records for driver/rider cancels are written with the waybill's quoted fare (`prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:212 'fare': record.fare`) and status `cancelled_by_*`/`searching`. The list is careful about this: earnings show '—' for non-completed rides (ride_history.dart:82) and the bonus note is guarded by `status == completed` (ride_history.dart:898). The detail contradicts it, presenting an amount and a bonus as the cost of a trip that ended with no fare.
failure_scenario: Driver cancels a 152,40 kr admin radar-group trip with a 40 kr bonus before pickup. History list shows '—'; opening it shows 'Ride cost 152,40 kr' and 'incl. +40 kr Movera bonus' above 'Cancelled by driver'.
evidence: line 400 `_detailRow(tr.rideCost, _ride.fare),` — line 402-407 `if (_ride.driverBonus case final bonus?) ...Text(WaybillRecord.bonusNote(bonus),` — ride_history.dart:82 `earnings: record.status == TripStatus.completed ? record.fare : '—',` — ride_history.dart:898-899 `if (ride.status == TripStatus.completed && ride.record.driverBonus != null)`
suggested_fix: Guard the fare row and the bonus note on `status == TripStatus.completed` (show '—' otherwise), matching the list.

title: Cash balance direction row is English-only ('You owe Movera') in the localized detail screen
description: The cash-trip rows use `cash.directionLabel`, which is `CashBalance.direction` returning hardcoded English strings (cash_balance.dart:46-50: 'You owe Movera' / 'Movera owes you' / 'Settled'). The surrounding rows (`tr.cashCollected`, `tr.cashMatchedYourFare`, `tr.settledInYourNextPayout`) are translated, so the Swedish/French screen mixes one English label into the money summary.
failure_scenario: Swedish driver opens a completed cash trip in History: 'Kontant insamlat 300,00 kr', then 'You owe Movera −51,60 kr', then the Swedish settlement note.
evidence: history_detail.dart:432 `child: _detailRow(cash.directionLabel, cash.signedLabel),` — cash_balance.dart:46-50 `static String direction(Money amount) => amount.minorUnits < 0 ? 'You owe Movera' : amount.minorUnits > 0 ? 'Movera owes you' : 'Settled';`
suggested_fix: Map the direction to `tr` keys at the presentation layer (the sheet already has `totalYouOweMovera`/`totalMoveraOwesYou`).

title: Overview counts and empty-state disagree about what a 'ride' is (cancelled trips counted in some places, not others)
description: `_periodRidesList` (line 100-111) contains every record with a `completedAt`, cancelled ones included. The overview's 'Rides' metric uses `_periodRides` (completed only, line 145), but the empty state `tr.noCompletedRidesInThisPeriod` is shown only when the whole list is empty (line 390), 'Latest rides' takes the first two of all records (line 392) and the button says `viewAllVisibleRideCountRides(_periodRidesList.length)` (line 306, 403). The All-rides summary row then says '{_periodRides} rides in {period}' while listing more cards.
failure_scenario: A week with 0 completed and 3 cancelled trips: Rides metric '0', no 'No completed rides in this period' text, two cancelled cards under Latest rides, button 'View all 3 rides', and the All rides header '0 rides in Last 7 days' above three cards.
evidence: line 145 `String get _periodRides => _periodRidesList.where((ride)=>ride.status==TripStatus.completed).length.toString();` — line 390 `if (_periodRidesList.isEmpty) Padding(..., child: Text(tr.noCompletedRidesInThisPeriod)),` — line 403 `label: Text(tr.viewAllVisibleRideCountRides(visibleRideCount)),` — line 448 `tr.periodRidesRidesInPeriodLabel(_periodRides, _periodLabel),`
suggested_fix: Decide one definition (all finished trips vs completed) and use it for the metric, the empty state, the count and the summary row.

title: All-rides list prints raw wire status names and a hardcoded 'cancelled_by_driver'
description: The non-compact history card shows `ride.status == completed ? tr.completed : ride.status.isReleasedToDispatch ? 'cancelled_by_driver' : ride.status.wireName`. Every non-completed outcome is therefore shown as its wire identifier with underscores (`cancelled_by_rider`, `no_show`, `expired`, `cancelled_by_system`) and the released-to-dispatch case as the literal `cancelled_by_driver`, in every language. The detail screen for the same record translates these (`_buildMetaRows`, history_detail.dart:455-467), so the list and the detail disagree.
failure_scenario: A rider cancels a trip. In History › All rides the card's status line reads `cancelled_by_rider`; tapping it shows 'Cancelled by rider'. In Swedish the list still shows the English snake_case token.
evidence: line 940 `ride.status == TripStatus.completed ? tr.completed : ride.status.isReleasedToDispatch ? 'cancelled_by_driver' : ride.status.wireName,`
suggested_fix: Reuse the outcome mapping from `_buildMetaRows` (or add a `TripStatus` → label helper) and show the translated outcome in the list.

title: Closing Radar while a claim is in flight drops a won trip
description: `_claimTrip` awaits `claimOffer` and then returns if `!mounted` (line 322) without handling the result. The Back button (`_closeRides`, line 270-282) stays enabled during Matching, and Home unmounts `RideRequests` on close (`showRideRequests = false`, home.dart:759-765, the whole Stack is replaced). `DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` removes the offer from the feed on success (line 565-566) and there is no other path that opens the accepted trip. So a Back tap during the ~1.45 s claim delay loses the trip: it is assigned (server side) but the driver never sees AcceptRide, and the card is gone from Radar when reopened.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Match, changes their mind and taps Back within a second, then reopens Radar: the trip is no longer listed (claim succeeded and removed it) and no active trip exists on this phone, while dispatch considers it accepted.
evidence: line 318 `result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(trip.id);` — line 322 `if (!mounted || _matchingOfferId != trip.id) { return; }` — line 567 (demo_dispatch_repository.dart) `_removeOffer(offerId); return ClaimResult.success(offer);` — home.dart:759-763 `onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; ...` (RideRequests is a child of the conditional Stack)
suggested_fix: Disable Back while `_matchingOfferId != null`, or hand a successful claim result to Home (callback/repository) so the active trip opens even when the Radar sheet has been closed.

title: Unknown rider rating is replaced by an invented 4.9 on the active ride screen
description: When a Radar match wins, `AcceptRide` is built with `riderRating: double.tryParse(rider.rating) ?? 4.9`. `RideOffer.rating` is a free string and is '' for reservations whose preview has no rating (`ReservationRequestPreview.rating` defaults to '', `RideOffer.reservation` copies it), so a trip with no known rating is shown to the driver as a 4.9-rated rider.
failure_scenario: An admin-created reservation without a rider rating joins Radar close to pickup; the driver matches it and the ride panel shows the rider as 4.9 stars.
evidence: line 379 `riderRating: double.tryParse(rider.rating) ?? 4.9,` — dispatch_repository.dart:65 `rating: reservation.rating,` — driver_home_admin_content.dart `this.rating = ''`
suggested_fix: Pass a nullable rating and hide the stars when it is unknown.

title: A withdrawal of another offer cancels the won-match timer: the claimed trip never opens and Radar is stuck in Matching
description: `_resolveMatchWon` (line 351-418) keeps the AcceptRide push on `_matchNoticeTimer` (500 ms). `_resolveMatchLost` (line 435) unconditionally does `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel()` for any trip, and `_onWithdrawn` (line 181-189) calls it for every `claimedElsewhere` withdrawal whose trip is still `available`. If dispatch withdraws trip B while trip A's win timer is pending, the timer is cancelled: `navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride))` never runs, `_matchingOfferId` stays A (line 437 only clears it when it equals B), `_offerStates[A]` stays `resolving`, so A's card shows the spinner forever and every other card's Match is disabled (`blockOtherOffers`, line 724-725). The server already removed A from the feed (`DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` line 565-566), so the trip is lost. Reproduced: match A, complete claim with success, pump 100 ms, emit `OfferWithdrawal(offerId: 'b', reason: claimedElsewhere)`, pump 2 s → `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`. The demo fires `withdrawOffer(radarGroupTaken)` on its own timer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:710-714), so the window is real, and a backend's `offer_withdrawn` can arrive at any moment.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Match on a Radar trip, dispatch answers success; within half a second another driver's accept withdraws a different card. The 'Matched' banner is replaced by 'Taken by another driver', no trip screen opens, the matched card spins forever, and no other trip can be matched until the driver closes and reopens Radar. The accepted trip is gone from the server feed.
evidence: line 366-368 `_matchNoticeTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 500), () { ... navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride));` — line 435 `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel();` in `_resolveMatchLost` — line 181-187 `void _onWithdrawn(OfferWithdrawal gone) { ... _resolveMatchLost(trip, _RadarGone.lostOwnMatch, notice: shown);` — test: `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`
suggested_fix: Use a separate timer for the won-match navigation (or push immediately and keep only the banner on a timer), and never let `_resolveMatchLost` for another offer touch the win timer; also ignore withdrawals while `_matchingOfferId` names a won trip.

title: Hardcoded English UI strings in localized screens
description: The app ships en/fr/sv (`lib/l10n/app_*.arb`) and every other label on these screens goes through `tr`, but several user-visible strings are literals: ride_requests.dart:648 `label: 'OFFERS'` on the live count badge; destination_picker.dart:361 `'${results.length} found'` under the search box; add_new_account.dart:253 section header `'ACCOUNT'`; analytics.dart:60 and driving_logs.dart:50 `'DEMO DATA'`; my_queue_pos.dart:121 `"15-30 mins EST time"` (also an abbreviation the driver cannot read). They stay English in Swedish and French.
failure_scenario: Driver language is French. Radar header shows '3 OFFERS', destination search shows '2 found', the bank form shows 'ACCOUNT', Analytics and Driving logs show 'DEMO DATA', the queue sheet shows '15-30 mins EST time'.
evidence: ride_requests.dart:648 `label: 'OFFERS',` — destination_picker.dart:361 `'${results.length} found',` — add_new_account.dart:253 `'ACCOUNT',` — analytics.dart:60 `'DEMO DATA',` — driving_logs.dart:50 `'DEMO DATA',` — my_queue_pos.dart:121 `text: "15-30 mins EST time",`
suggested_fix: Move each string into the ARB files and read it through `tr`.

title: On web, 'Dialer opened' is reported for tel:112 because url_launcher_web returns true unconditionally
description: handoffEmergencyDial maps `launch()` true to EmergencyDialResult.opened, and the Safety toolkit then shows tr.safetyDialerOpened; RideCheckController.callEmergency likewise sets `_dialOpened = true` and moves the card to the 'called' state.
