The default launcher is `launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))`. url_launcher_web (2.4.3, url_launcher_web.dart:66-69, 112-115) documents that launchUrl 'Always returns true, except for disallowed schemes' because window.open with noopener cannot report success; on a desktop browser (or a mobile browser with no tel handler) nothing opens, yet the UI confirms the dialer opened. REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md's product-truth gate forbids claiming an action succeeded when it did not.
failure_scenario: Driver using the PWA on a laptop/desktop (or a tablet without telephony) taps Call 112 -> browser does nothing or shows a silent protocol prompt -> app shows 'Dialer opened' / ride-check card advances to 'Called 112' with alertSent, though no call path exists.
evidence: safety_toolkits.dart:87-97 `final result = await handoffEmergencyDial(widget.launchEmergencyDial ?? () => launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))); ... _showMessage(result == EmergencyDialResult.opened ? tr.safetyDialerOpened : tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112);`; ride_check_controller.dart:166-171 `final result = await handoffEmergencyDial(() => services.launch(RideCheckServices.emergencyNumber)); ... _dialOpened = result == EmergencyDialResult.opened;`; url_launcher_web.dart:66-69 `/// Always returns true, except for disallowed schemes. Because noopener ... opened successfully.`
suggested_fix: On web, phrase the confirmation neutrally ('Opening 112…' / show the number to dial) instead of asserting the dialer opened, or gate the success copy on `!kIsWeb`.

title: 'PIN verification' tile title is hardcoded although tr.pinVerification exists
description: In the Safety preferences sheet the first tile title is the literal `'PIN verification'` while its subtitle and the other tiles use `tr`. The key `pinVerification` exists in all three arb files (en 'Pin verification', fr 'Vérification par code') and is used by settings.dart:95, so this sheet shows English in fr/sv and even a different English spelling from Settings.
failure_scenario: Language Français > Settings > Safety > Safety preferences: tile reads 'PIN verification' with a French subtitle.
evidence: safety_toolkits.dart:177-180 `_preferenceTile( icon: Icons.pin_outlined, title: 'PIN verification', subtitle: tr.safetyUnavailableWithoutVerification,`; app_fr.arb:481 `"pinVerification": "Vérification par code"`
suggested_fix: Use `tr.pinVerification`.

title: Safety toolkit status banner shows a green success check for 'Could not open the dialer' and 'unavailable' messages
description: `_status` is rendered in one fixed style: green background `0xFFE7F4EE` and `Icons.check_circle_outline_rounded` in green (lines 440-471). `_confirmEmergencyCall` puts `tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112` ('Could not open the dialer. Dial 112 manually.') into the same banner when `handoffEmergencyDial` returns `unavailable`, and `_toggleRecording`/`_shareTrip` put 'Audio recording is unavailable in this demo.' there. The failure of the only real action in the sheet (112 dial) is thus visually confirmed as success.
failure_scenario: On a device/browser where `launchUrl(Uri.parse('tel:112'))` returns false (web, tablet without telephony), tap Contact 112 > Call 112: a green check banner appears reading 'Could not open the dialer...'.
evidence: safety_toolkits.dart:93-97 `_showMessage(result == EmergencyDialResult.opened ? tr.safetyDialerOpened : tr.couldNotOpenDialerDial112);` and :452-455 `const Icon(Icons.check_circle_outline_rounded, color: _green, size: 17,)`
suggested_fix: Carry a severity with `_status` (info/error) and style the banner/icon accordingly.

title: Reservation claim that succeeds after the list unmounts is lost and later reported 'No longer available'
description: `_claim` awaits `dispatch.claimOffer(ride.id)` (line 273) with the list screen's Back button active (`_buildHeader`, line 310-313). On success after unmount it returns false (line 278) and `_openRideDetails` stops before `_requests.remove`/`_accepted.insert` (line 222-224). The demo dispatch has already removed the reservation from `_reservations` and the Radar feed (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:537-544). The ride stays in the store's Requests; the next Accept calls `claimOffer` again, which now returns `unavailable` (line 559-560), so `_claim` runs `ScheduledRideStore.take(ride.id)` and shows 'No longer available' (line 286-291) to the driver who actually won it. The same path is hit when `_requests.remove(ride)` at line 223 fails because the request left the store while the claim was pending.
failure_scenario: Driver taps Accept on an open reservation and presses Back during the claim. Later they open Scheduled rides, see the reservation still under Requests, tap Accept, and get 'No longer available'. The reservation was assigned to them by dispatch and never reaches the Accepted tab, so no reminder, 'leave now' or waybill will come.
evidence: line 273 `result = await dispatch.claimOffer(ride.id);` — line 278 `if (!mounted) return false;` — line 222-223 `if (!await _claim(ride) || !mounted) return; if (!ScheduledRideStore._requests.remove(ride)) return;` — demo_dispatch_repository.dart:537-544 `final reservation = _reservations.remove(offerId); if (reservation != null) { ... return ... ClaimResult.success(reservation); }`
suggested_fix: Move the claim and the store mutation into `ScheduledRideStore` (not the widget) so a successful claim always moves the ride to Accepted regardless of the screen's lifetime; disable Back while `_claiming` is non-empty.

title: Sample accepted ride is seeded with a localized pickupDay, so its time logic silently differs by language
description: `_seedAccepted` sets `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow` on the `ReservationRequestPreview` (line 445). `pickupAt` only recognises the English keys 'today'/'tomorrow' (driver_home_admin_content.dart:246-251), so in Swedish ('Imorgon') or French the sample ride has `pickupAt == null`. Consequences inside this screen: `_clashWith` never treats it as clashing (smart_gap.dart:88-90 returns false), so the clash filter and the 'rides hidden' note behave differently from English; `freeCancelUntil` returns null so the cancel sheet shows the generic 'free X hours before' line instead of the real time and `isLateCancel` is never true; `upcoming` (line 626-634) excludes it so Home's reminders/leave-now never fire for it. The existing test (scheduled_rides_rules_test.dart:112) only asserts the English behaviour.
failure_scenario: In Swedish, a request whose time clashes with the sample 08:15 ride is still listed and can be accepted, and cancelling the sample ride 30 minutes before pickup is not counted as late; in English the same actions are blocked/counted.
evidence: line 445 `pickupDay: tr.tomorrow,` — driver_home_admin_content.dart:247-249 `final day = pickupDay.trim().toLowerCase(); final offset = day == 'today' ? 0 : day == 'tomorrow' ? 1 : null;` — smart_gap.dart:88-90 `if (a.pickupAt(now) == null || b.pickupAt(now) == null) { return false; }`
suggested_fix: Seed the model with the English key ('Tomorrow') and localize only for display (`ReservationWhen.dayWord`).

title: Scheduled ride cards show English 'Today'/'Tomorrow' in the Swedish and French UI
description: `_ScheduledRide.request` (line 1134) and `_ScheduledRide.fromRoute` (line 1117) format the card time with `tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime)` using the model's raw English day key ('Today'/'Tomorrow', see `_DemoReservationSet._at` and `pickupAt`'s parsing of 'today'/'tomorrow'). The app has a localizer for exactly this (`ReservationWhen.dayWord`, reservation_when.dart:89-93, used by reservation_route_map.dart:427) but these two constructors do not use it. Every real request and every accepted ride in the list therefore reads 'Today, 07:40–07:45' / 'Tomorrow, 08:15' under Swedish or French.
failure_scenario: Driver language is Swedish. Scheduled rides lists 'Today, 07:40–07:45' and 'Tomorrow, 08:15' while the header, tabs and notes are Swedish; the same label is used in the details hero (line 1518).
evidence: line 1117 `time: tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime),` — line 1134 `var time = tr.schedSeedTime(route.pickupDay, route.pickupTime);` — reservation_when.dart:89-91 `static String dayWord(String day) => switch (day.trim().toLowerCase()) { 'today' => tr.today, 'tomorrow' => tr.tomorrow, ...`
suggested_fix: Pass `ReservationWhen.dayWord(route.pickupDay)` to `schedSeedTime` in both constructors.

title: 'tomorrow' is dropped from the free-cancel time on the spring DST day
description: `_timeFrom` computes the day gap as `DateTime(y,m,d).difference(DateTime(y,m,d)).inDays`. On the day DST starts, local midnight to next local midnight is 23 h, so `inDays` is 0 and a time that is tomorrow is rendered as a bare clock ('07:15') instead of 'tomorrow 07:15'. Used by `_freeCancelLine` for `schedFreeCancelUntil` in the details plan card (scheduled_rides.dart:1705) and the cancel sheet (`_CancelRulesBox`). Reproduced in TZ=Europe/Stockholm: now 28 Mar 2027 12:00, until 29 Mar 07:00 → `inDays=0`.
failure_scenario: On the last Sunday of March the driver opens an accepted ride for tomorrow 08:15. The plan card says 'Free cancel until 07:15.' with no day, which reads as today 07:15 (already passed), so the driver believes any cancel is now late.
evidence: scheduled_rides_notes.dart:11-13 `final days = DateTime(time.year, time.month, time.day).difference(DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays;` — line 15-19 `return days == 0 ? clock : days == 1 ? tr.tomorrowAtClock(clock) : ...` — test: `spring: offsets now=2:00 until=2:00 inDays=0`
suggested_fix: Compare calendar dates (`DateUtils.dateOnly` and compute the day number difference in UTC), e.g. `DateTime.utc(time.year, time.month, time.day).difference(DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays`.

title: Settings re-runs MapTrafficSetting.restore on open; a quick toggle of 'Show traffic' is reverted in the UI while the opposite value is saved
description: `MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings)` is fired unawaited in `initState` although main.dart:41 already restored it at startup. The restore enqueues a read; if the driver flips the switch before that read resolves, `MapTrafficSetting.set` sets `enabled.value` immediately and enqueues the save behind the read. When the read completes it overwrites `enabled.value` with the old stored value, so the switch snaps back, while the queued save then writes the driver's new value. UI and storage disagree until the next restore.
failure_scenario: Open Settings and immediately tap 'Show traffic on map' off: the switch flips back to ON; relaunch the app and it is OFF.
evidence: settings.dart:33-36 `void initState() { super.initState(); MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings); }`; map_traffic_setting.dart `restore`: `enabled.value = saved is bool ? saved : defaultValue;` after the await; `set`: `enabled.value = value; return ... .save(section, {key: value});`
suggested_fix: Drop the restore in Settings (startup already restores) or have `restore` skip applying when a `set` happened after it started.

title: When Maps JavaScript (or the adapter) never loads on web, the map stays a blank beige box forever with no error state and a 50 ms poll that never stops
description: On web `_mapsReady` starts as `web.ready`, which is false until `google.maps` is installed by driver_map_camera.js. If the Maps script never arrives (ad/privacy blocker, key referrer rejection returning an error script, captive portal, offline PWA start) the widget keeps a `Timer.periodic(50 ms)` running for its whole lifetime and renders `ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land)` indefinitely. Nothing surfaces the failure to the driver: Home's own 8 s `_startWaitLimit` only covers the start position, not the SDK, and no caller of CustomGoogleMap can observe the not-ready state. The driver sees a flat colour where the map should be, with markers, routes and offer previews silently missing, and the DemoModeBanner/offer flow continue as if the map existed.
failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA with a content blocker that blocks maps.googleapis.com -> Home shows the beige placeholder forever, 'Finding your location' resolves, offers arrive, but no map, route or car is ever drawn and no message explains why; the 50 ms timer keeps polling until the screen is disposed.
evidence: custom_google_map.dart:273-286 `bool _mapsReady = web.ready; Timer? _mapsReadyPoll; ... _mapsReadyPoll = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 50), (timer) { if (!web.ready) return; timer.cancel(); if (mounted) setState(() => _mapsReady = true); });`; custom_google_map.dart:407-408 `if (!_mapsReady) const ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land) else GoogleMap(`; driver_map_web_bridge.dart:11-17 `bool get ready { final adapter = _adapter; if (adapter == null) return false; ...}`
suggested_fix: Bound the wait (e.g. 10-15 s) and then show a 'Map unavailable' state / retry, or expose an onUnavailable callback so Home and AcceptRide can tell the driver.

title: With reduced motion (and on the far-cut path) a GPS retarget that arrives during the single moveCamera await is dropped: retarget() requires _looping but _run has already captured the goal, and the controller nulls its pending pose after calling retarget
description: `animate()` marks `_looping = true` and starts `_run`. In the `reducedMotion || _logical == null` branch `_run` reads `initial = _goal`, awaits one `_move(...)` and returns; the same happens on the `_far` cut (`await _move(destination ...); break;`). While that `moveCamera` platform call is in flight the controller still sees `_busy == true`, so a new fix goes through `_request` → `_port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null;` (driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737). `retarget` stores the pose in `_goal` (it passes the `_looping` check), but nobody reads `_goal` again: `_run` returns, `finally` clears `_looping`, the session completes, the controller sets `_busy = false` and arms a 16 ms throttle with `_pending` already null. The fix is lost until the next one, so under reduced motion the car/camera skip fixes whenever a platform round-trip overlaps a GPS event. Narrow window (a few ms per fix) but a real contract break of `DriverCameraPort.retarget` ('the in-flight animation steers toward this pose').
failure_scenario: Driver with 'reduce motion' enabled on a 1 Hz GPS trip: occasionally a fix lands while the previous moveCamera is awaiting acknowledgement; that fix never reaches the map and the camera holds the previous position for an extra second.
evidence: google_driver_camera_port.dart:259-263: `if (reducedMotion || _logical == null) { await _move(_at(initial, initial.target), trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); return; }`; :283-287: `if (_far(from, destination)) { _flightPending = false; await _move(destination, trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); break; }`; :223-229: `void retarget(DriverCameraPose pose) { if (_disposed || !_looping) { return; } _goal = pose; ...`. driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737: `if (_busy && pending != null) { _port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null; }`.
suggested_fix: After the single move / far cut, re-check `_goal` and issue one more `_move` if it changed during the await (or keep `_pending` in the controller until the port confirms it consumed the retarget).

title: Counter badges show hard-coded English 'NEW' (default label) on Scheduled rides and 'OFFERS' on Ride requests
description: `LedCountBadge` renders `label` as visible text (line 72-80). `scheduled_rides.dart:169` uses the default `label = 'NEW'`; `ride_requests.dart:648` passes `label: 'OFFERS'`. The ARB already has `rrNew`/`orbNew` and `allOffers` (used by home_offer_radar.dart:1102), so these two sites were simply missed. Reproduced in the Swedish dump of Scheduled rides: `... 88, 02, NEW, 126.75 kr ...`.
failure_scenario: Swedish/French driver sees 'NEW' beside the request count on Bokade resor and 'OFFERS' on the Radar list.
evidence: led_count_badge.dart:12: `this.label = 'NEW',` — scheduled_rides.dart:169: `LedCountBadge(count: _requests.length),` — ride_requests.dart:645-648: `LedCountBadge( key: const ValueKey<String>('radar-live-count'), count: count, label: 'OFFERS',`
suggested_fix: Pass `tr.orbNew`/`tr.rrNew` and `tr.allOffers` (or a new `offers` key).

title: Evidence-matrix test forbids any PASS row, so recording real evidence breaks CI
description: The test asserts `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')))` on docs/certification/RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md. That freezes the current all-PENDING state as a rule: the first legitimately PASSed check (with an artifact, which tool/check_evidence_matrix.py explicitly supports) makes `flutter test` fail in the verify job. The test does not verify the matrix's correctness; it verifies that no progress has been made.
failure_scenario: The team completes the layout certification, records `| PASS |` with an artifact path; drider-ci verify job fails on evidence_matrix_test and the only ways out are deleting the test or lying in the matrix.
evidence: test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:17 `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')));`
suggested_fix: Replace with 'PASS rows must have an artifact' (or delegate to check_evidence_matrix.py) instead of forbidding PASS.

title: Vacuous assertion: GoogleMap property check after asserting no GoogleMap exists
description: After `expect(find.byType(GoogleMap), findsNothing)` the test iterates `tester.widgetList<GoogleMap>(find.byType(GoogleMap)).any(...)` and expects false; with no GoogleMap widgets `any` is always false, so the second assertion can never fail and does not verify the start-position property it appears to cover.
failure_scenario: The Home map starts rendering at a wrong initial camera position; this assertion still passes because the list it inspects is empty by construction.
evidence: test/audit/home_start_position_test.dart:81-85 `expect(find.byType(GoogleMap), findsNothing);` followed by `expect(tester.widgetList<GoogleMap>(find.byType(GoogleMap)).any(...), isFalse);`
suggested_fix: Assert the initial camera position on the real map widget once it is built (or drop the dead assertion).

title: Test titled 'the Home sound releases the player it made' asserts the player is NOT released
description: The test name promises coverage of the D-17 ownership rule (a player created by the Home sound is disposed by it), but it injects a player and then asserts `expect(audio.released, isFalse)` with the comment 'An injected player belongs to whoever passed it in'. The path where the sound creates its own player and must dispose it is never exercised, so a leak of the self-made AudioPlayer (and its platform channel / audio session) would not be caught, while the test title tells reviewers it is.
failure_scenario: A refactor stops disposing the internally created AudioPlayer on Home dispose; every test stays green; drivers accumulate live audio players across Home re-creations (sound keeps playing / memory grows).
evidence: test/core/radar_offer_sound_test.dart:92 `test('D-17: the Home sound releases the player it made', () async {` ... :101 `expect(audio.released, isFalse);`
suggested_fix: Rename this case to 'an injected player is not released' and add a second case that lets the sound build its own player via a factory hook and asserts dispose is called.

title: 37 bare tester.takeException() calls silently discard flow exceptions in widget tests
description: Across 15 widget test files (account_flow_test.dart x10, offer_rules_flow_test.dart x7, reservation_near_pickup_test.dart x5, radar_offer_gone_test.dart x3, d3_trip_options_test.dart x2, and one each in round3/driver_admin_offers_home_test, offer_rules_cards_test, d3_home_back_test, radar_offer_close_test, d11_home_map_keep_test, home_offer_route_test, reservation_request_popup_test, exclusive_sheet_test, home_scheduled_test, adaptive_trip_island_test) a bare `tester.takeException();` is placed before tear-down or before the real assertions. It consumes any FlutterError raised during the flow (overflows, setState after dispose, null errors in build) without checking it, so layout regressions in Home/account/offer flows cannot fail these tests. In d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 the comment even states the trip screen itself overflows at the tested sizes ('Layout of the trip screen itself is not what this test covers.').
failure_scenario: A change introduces a RenderFlex overflow or a 'setState() called after dispose()' in the Home account menu; account_flow_test's ten cases still pass because the exception is swallowed at lines 242/263/304/347/359/386/411/427/442/490.
evidence: grep count: 37 occurrences of `^\s*tester.takeException();` across 15 files; test/widget/d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 `// Layout of the trip screen itself is not what this test covers.\ntester.takeException();`; test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:472 `tester.takeException();`
suggested_fix: Replace bare calls with `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` where the flow is expected to be clean, or assert the specific expected exception type; fix the underlying trip-screen overflow referenced in d3_trip_options_test.

title: PASS evidence accepted with any non-empty artifact string; artifact path existence is never checked
description: A PASS row only has to carry a non-empty `artifact` string; the script never verifies that the path exists in the repository or is a URL. A typo'd or deleted artifact path therefore still counts as evidence, and with --require-complete the release would be declared complete on the strength of a string. The companion script tool/check_evidence_matrix.py has the same shape (PASS requires a non-empty artifact cell only).
failure_scenario: Someone records status PASS with artifact 'docs/evidence/layout.png' that was never committed; both gates stay green and the release is signed off on missing evidence.
evidence: tool/check_frontend_release.py:46-48 `artifact = row.get("artifact")\nif not isinstance(artifact, str) or not artifact.strip():\n    raise ValueError(f"{check}: PASS requires an artifact")`
suggested_fix: Resolve `artifact` relative to the repo root (or accept http(s) URLs) and fail when the file does not exist.

title: The web verifier stubs MutationObserver as a no-op, so the documented 'listeners and overlays are released when their map is disposed' path in driver_map_camera.js is never executed
description: docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:77-78 and :87-89 claim the adapter releases Flutter listeners and the vehicle overlay when the map is disposed and that `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` covers 'listener removal'. The adapter implements disposal with a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (`driver_map_camera.js:501-510`: `state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect();`). The verifier's context defines `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}` and never toggles `div.isConnected`, so that callback cannot run; the only 'removal' asserted is the explicit unsubscribe returned by `listen()` (`cjs:477-479`). A regression in the disconnect cleanup (e.g. a stale `states` entry keeping a disposed map and its gesture callbacks alive across a map re-create) would pass CI.
failure_scenario: A change that breaks the disconnect cleanup in driver_map_camera.js ships green; after a Home map re-create the old map's JS state keeps calling the previous Flutter gesture callback and holding the old overlay.
evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:72: `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}};`; :477-479: `remove(); const count = gestures; div.fire('pointerdown', [], mouse(100,100)); ... assert.equal(gestures,count,'Disposed Flutter listener released');`. web/driver_map_camera.js:503-509: `const observer = new MutationObserver(() => { wasConnected ||= div.isConnected; if (wasConnected && !div.isConnected) { state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect(); } });`. docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:87-89: `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs (CI): ... vehicle overlay and listener removal.`
suggested_fix: Give the verifier a MutationObserver double that captures the callback, set `div.isConnected = false`, invoke it, and assert `states` no longer serves the id (configure/listen become no-ops) and that the overlay/car `setMap(null)` ran.

title: Final anchor/look-ahead/sheet-glide contract assertions run only inside nested queueMicrotask callbacks; script exits 0 if the chain never runs
description: Lines 607-649 wrap the last group of assertions (claim/anchor, look-ahead, sheet glide, locate view) in five nested queueMicrotask callbacks, and the only 'PASS: ...' log is at the innermost level (line 644). Nothing at top level records that the callbacks executed (no counter, no process.on('exit') check, no explicit process.exitCode set when the PASS line is not reached). If a future adapter change causes an earlier await/microtask to never resolve, or an exception inside the mocks is caught by the adapter, the script finishes with exit 0 and the CI step `node tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` (drider-ci.yml:58) stays green with those contracts unverified.
failure_scenario: driver_map_camera.js changes so that the claim() path returns before scheduling the pan; the nested callbacks' assertions never execute; CI reports success and the look-ahead/sheet-glide regression ships to Pages.
evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:607 `queueMicrotask(() => {` ... :619, :626, :633, :641 nested `queueMicrotask(() => {`; :644 `console.log('PASS: vector palette, ... locate view');` (only completion marker)
suggested_fix: Set a `done = false` flag, flip it after the innermost assertions, and add `process.on('exit', () => { if (!done) { console.error('FAIL: async contracts did not run'); process.exitCode = 1; } })`.
